museum.jpg|サムネイル|宗像大社辺津宮 神宝館]] === 宗像大社辺津宮 === * 本殿（第一宮、イチキシマヒメを御祭神とする。{{jalink|宗像氏貞|Q10204112}}の建立で、大島に在する中津宮の本殿を参考したといわれる。重文） * 拝殿（切妻屋根、宗像宮の額がかかる。{{jalink|小早川隆景|Q1143508}}の建立。重文） * 第二宮（沖津宮分社、タゴリヒメを御祭神とする。） * 第三宮（中津宮分社、タギツヒメを御祭神とする。） * 高宮祭場（邊津宮に於ける古代祭祀遺構、下高宮祭祀遺跡を保護し真上に新たに整備。現在も春と秋の大祭他、庭上祭祀が行われている。） * 祈願殿（平成の大造営で新たに建築された。榊を中心に植え、岩を沖ノ島に見立てた庭が作庭され、窓口では各種祈願を受け付ける。） * 儀式殿（結婚式など催事専用の殿舎。以前東京の靖国神社にあったものを移築。） * 清明殿（宗像大社の巫女らが舞などを披露する殿舎。） * 勅使館（天皇や皇族、その勅使らが奉幣に来社の際、滞在する殿舎。） * 神門（大正期に再建。） * 握舎（拝殿と神門を結ぶ参道上に新しく設けられた屋根、覆い。現在「神門」が拝殿正面になり、拝殿及び本殿ともに横からしか見えない。） * 祓舎（祓戸神を四方に祀る。） * 手水舎（{{jalink|柄杓|Q11533616}}がなく直接水を受ける。） * 大鳥居（{{jalink|麻生太吉|Q2743525}}の寄進。） * 末社（江戸時代初期の建立、神郡宗像にあった神社群を時の福岡藩主、{{jalink|黒田光之|Q11678571}}がまとめ寄進したもので、本殿の外周りに121社ほどある。） * 蛭子社 * 松尾社 * 宗像祖霊社 * 宗像護国神社 * 神宝館（下記記載の国宝等を展示収蔵して愉いる。） * むなかた茶愉（カフェ併設の休憩施設。アート作品の展示販売も行っている。） === 宗像大社中津宮 === * 本殿（宗像氏貞の建立。屋根の千木は{{jalink|陰陽道|Q1340540}}の影響がみられる。昔の{{jalink|吉田神道|Q1760351}}では宗像神社を特別な神社とみていた影響とも言われる。現在の辺津宮本殿よりも歴史は古くモデルとされたとする説もある。県重文。） * 拝殿（切妻屋根。福岡藩主黒田氏の再建。） * 奥宮{{jalink|御嶽神社|Q11488964}}（中津宮における古代祭祀遺構、多数の勾玉や鉄刀が出土。現在も祭事が行われている。） * 織女社、牽牛社（天の川を挟んで建てられた石の祠形式の社。中津宮は日本の{{jalink|七夕|Q13423122}}伝説発祥の地ともいう。） === 宗像大社沖津宮 === * 社殿（三宮の社殿では一番小さく、屋根が巨岩にめり込むように建てられている。） * 禊場、沖津宮社務所など === 沖津宮遙拝所 === * 遥拝殿 （彼方に御神体島の沖ノ島及び沖津宮を拝する銅板葺き破風付きの社殿。福岡藩主黒田氏の寄進。） * 鳥居、他 === 歴史 === {{jalink|伝承|Q36192}}では{{jalink|日本神話|Q814158}}に{{jalink|起源}}を持つ。{{jalink|天照大神|Q455602}}と{{jalink|スサノオ|Q272993|素戔嗚尊}}の{{jalink|アマテラスとスサノオの誓約|Q11284880|誓約}}（うけい）の際、天照大神が素戔嗚の剣を噛み砕き、プッと吹き出した破片から生まれたのが宗像三女神である。女神たちはアマテラスの'''{{jalink|神勅|Q11588781}}'''を奉じて、皇孫{{jalink|ニニギノミコト}}を見守り助けるため海北道中、玄界灘に浮かぶ筑紫宗像の島々に降り、この地を治めるようになったのが宗像大社の起源とする。{{jalink|記紀|Q842308}}に記載される「天から地に降りた神」は{{jalink|ニニギノミコト}}とその{{jalink|天孫降臨|Q1084733}}以前に天降った宗像三女神だけである。これは記紀に記載される神名とその鎮座地が明確に記述されたものとしては最古のものである。宗像三宮の御神体依代について、{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}{{jalink|風土記|Q1194534}}に依れば、『西海道風土記曰、宗像大神、自天降居埼門山之時以、青玉置奧津宮之表以、八尺紫玉置中津宮之表以、八咫鏡置邊津宮之表以、此三表成神體之形而納置三宮、即隱之因曰身形郡後人改曰、宗像其大海命子孫、今宗像朝臣等是也云々』と逸文に記述あり。宗像は『{{jalink|古事記|Q813031}}』では胸形という字が当てられ、また胸肩、宗形とも表記されるが、もとは水潟であったとする説もある。古くから当地の民の氏神として信仰を集めてきたが、{{jalink|神功皇后|Q232803}}が{{jalink|三韓征伐|Q11249435}}の際ここに航海の安全を祈り霊験があったといわれ、事あるごとに宗像に奉幣使を派遣する習いになったとされる。{{jalink|大和朝廷}}から重視され、古来{{jalink|遷都|Q558566}}の度に宮中の{{jalink|賢所|Q11635085}}（かしこどころ）に当社の分霊が奉斎された。またこの逸話からは航海安全の{{jalink|守護神|Q131278957}}として崇められるようになった経緯がうかがえる。 {{jalink|律令制#日本の律令制|Q742460|律令制}}導入により{{jalink|国郡里制|Q11421491|国郡制}}が布かれると{{jalink|宗像郡|Q6935606|宗像一郡}}が{{jalink|寺社領|Q11458058|神領}}として与えられ、当地の{{jalink|豪族|Q84066}}{{jalink|宗像氏|Q16481907|宗形氏}}が{{jalink|神職|Q60523|神主}}として神社に奉仕し、{{jalink|神郡|Q11590937}}の{{jalink|行政|Q31728}}も司ることになった。宗形氏の由緒を記した{{jalink|石碑|Q178743}}によれば、宗形氏の族長が二代にわたって中国の{{jalink|商人|Q215536}}の娘を{{jalink|正室|Q1765533}}に迎えている。また{{jalink|宗形徳善|Q11451927}}は娘の{{jalink|尼子娘|Q11464914}}を{{jalink|天武天皇|Q335181}}の{{jalink|後宮|Q5353683}}に入れ、{{jalink|白雉|Q540118}}5年（{{jalink|654年|Q31109}}）に二人の間に生まれた第一皇子{{jalink|高市皇子|Q837590}}は{{jalink|壬申の乱|Q2378252}}で父を助けて大功を挙げ、のちに{{jalink|太政大臣|Q1157586}}に任ぜられた。{{jalink|長屋王|Q1963492}}は高市の子であり、また{{jalink|高階氏|Q11673216}}の祖ともなった。{{jalink|807年|Q30016}}（{{jalink|大同 (日本)|Q1373191|大同}}2年）には{{jalink|封戸|Q11458391}}74戸の寄進、{{jalink|840年|Q29936}}（{{jalink|承和 (日本)|Q1075605|承和}}7年）には{{jalink|従五位下}}に叙され後、{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}（{{jalink|貞観 (日本)|Q1075635|貞観}}元年）、{{jalink|正二位|Q11123277}}となる。{{jalink|天慶|Q1327340}}4年（{{jalink|天慶の乱|Q11442602}}後）には更に進めて{{jalink|正一位|Q11123258}}の{{jalink|神階|Q11591025}}を得る。{{jalink|979年|Q23784}}（{{jalink|天元 (日本)|Q1327101|天元}}2年）{{jalink|大宮司}}職が{{jalink|太政官|Q1192939}}より定められる。 {{jalink|鎌倉時代|Q236205}}以降、宗形氏の後身で大宮司家の地位を世襲した{{jalink|宗像氏|Q16481907}}が武士化し、有力な国人領主に成長したが、戦国時代には{{jalink|大内氏|Q1348909}}・{{jalink|大友氏|Q1096662}}・{{jalink|少弐氏|Q2975368}}など近隣の大名同士の戦争に動員され、宗像大社も軍事攻撃の対象となってたびたび放火・破壊を受け、その宗像氏も衰退していった。しかしそのつど{{jalink|朝廷 (日本)|Q30253177|朝廷}}や{{jalink|武家|Q2927809}}の信奉があり再建を繰り返してきた。こけら葺きの大屋根が美しい現在の辺津宮{{jalink|本殿|Q2044994}}は、天正6年（{{jalink|1578年|Q6707}}）に大宮司{{jalink|宗像氏貞|Q10204112}}が再建、辺津宮{{jalink|拝殿|Q3125745}}は、筑前領主であった{{jalink|小早川隆景|Q1143508}}によって天正16年（{{jalink|1590年|Q6764}}）に再建された。辺津宮の本殿拝殿ともに国の{{jalink|重要文化財|Q1188622}}に指定されている。宗像氏が担ってきた祭祀はその後、{{jalink|草刈氏}}（{{jalink|草刈重継|Q22126274}}）に引き継がれた。江戸時代には{{jalink|筑前|Q242409}}{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766}}主{{jalink|黒田氏|Q2975305}}などによる社殿の造営・修理、社領の{{jalink|寄進|Q11455717}}などが度々伝えられている。その後、幕末から明治の{{jalink|廃仏毀釈|Q702298}}により{{jalink|神宮寺|Q1074971}}であった屏風山{{jalink|鎮国寺|Q11651157}}は大社から切り離された。 また、{{jalink|1871年|Q7746}} ({{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}4年）には{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534}}において「宗像神社」として{{jalink|国幣中社}}に列した。その翌年の4月22日、{{jalink|官幣中社}}に昇格。そして{{jalink|1901年|Q2035}}（{{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}34年）7月11日、最高位の{{jalink|近代社格制度#官社|Q712534|官幣大社}}に昇格した。 {{jalink|昭和|Q327567}}の{{jalink|第二次世界大戦|Q362}}の後、荒廃していた境内は赤間（宗像市赤間地区）出身で、幼い頃より宗像大社を崇敬していた実業家、{{jalink|出光佐三|Q7429431}}の寄進により整備され、沖津宮のある沖ノ島祭祀遺跡の調査発掘に際しては国に働きかけるなど尽力している。 === 行幸啓 === {{jalink|1983年|Q2434}}（{{jalink|昭和|Q327567}}58年）、皇太子明仁親王（後の{{jalink|上皇明仁||明仁上皇}}）と美智子同妃（後の{{jalink|上皇后美智子|Q87610}}）が辺津宮へ参拝した。 {{jalink|2013年|Q1998}}（{{jalink|平成|Q234510}}25年）、{{jalink|徳仁|Q217096|皇太子徳仁親王}}が辺津宮へ参拝した。 {{jalink|2017年|Q25290}}（平成29年）{{jalink|10月29日|Q2951}}、明仁天皇・美智子皇后が、歴代の天皇・皇后として初めて辺津宮へ{{jalink|親拝}}した{{Cite news|和書|title=福岡）両陛下が世界遺産登録の宗像大社を参拝：朝日新聞デジタル|url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASKBY5R38KBYTIPE012.html|accessdate=2018-05-08|language=ja-JP|work=朝日新聞デジタル}}{{リンク切れ|date=2024年3月}}。 なお、皇室の参拝としては{{jalink|昭和天皇|Q34479}}の弟で{{jalink|考古学者|Q3621491}}でもあった{{jalink|三笠宮崇仁親王|Q280229}}は幾度も参拝しており、沖ノ島の和歌も詠んでいる。 === 摂社 === * 神湊宗像神社（古宮）- 境外摂社（秋季大祭田島放生会、{{jalink|みあれ祭|Q11278738}}で三女神の神輿が並び奉斎される） === 神事・祭事 === * 新年祭 - 歳旦祭など新年正月を祝う神事。毎年正月1～3日。 * 春季大祭 - 毎年4月1〜3日。 * 夏越大祓 - 毎年7月終わりに行われる。 * {{jalink|七夕|Q13423122}}祭 - 毎年{{jalink|旧暦|Q11511066}}7月7日夕刻時、{{jalink|筑前大島}}の中津宮末社で行われる。{{jalink|牽牛}}社・{{jalink|織女}}社というのがあり、その前に短冊を付けた竹笹を立てて技芸の上達を祈る。水に映る姿を見て男女の因縁を占う神事や、七夕{{jalink|揮毫|Q11498466}}大会も開かれる。正平年中行事によると、{{jalink|1346年|Q6080}}「七月七日之七夕虫振神事」とある。 * 秋季大祭 - 毎年10月1〜3日。1〜3日の辺津宮本殿での催しに先立って中津宮・沖津宮で{{jalink|神迎え}}の神事があり、漁船群の立てる色とりどりの旗や幟で{{jalink|神幸||海上神幸}}を行う（みあれ祭）。本殿では{{jalink|翁|Q11610439}}舞、風俗舞、{{jalink|流鏑馬|Q1886157}}、奉納{{jalink|相撲|Q40561}}などが披露される。起源は{{jalink|平安時代|Q193292}}にまで遡るといい、正式名称は「田島放生会」と呼ぶ。 * 献茶祭 - 毎年10月17日に開催される。 * 豊穣祭 - 平成の天皇・皇后が当社に親拝したのを機に毎年催行されるようになった新しい祭事。 * 西日本菊花大会 - 毎年11月に開催される菊花展。九州はもとより西日本各県から園芸栽培された菊花が多数展示され品評される。 * 古式祭、鎮火祭 - 毎年12月中旬に行われる800年以上の歴史を持つ冬の秘祭。 * 年越大祓 - 毎年大晦日に行われる除夜の神事。 === 文化財 === === 国宝 === * '''福岡県宗像大社沖津宮祭祀遺跡出土品・伝福岡県宗像大社沖津宮祭祀遺跡出土品''' 一括 : 玄界灘に浮かぶ絶海の孤島・沖ノ島の20数箇所の祭祀遺跡から発掘された一括遺物。{{jalink|1954年|Q18581}}から{{jalink|1971年|Q2475}}に至る第1次〜第3次の{{jalink|発掘調査|Q959782}}で出土したもので、時代的には{{jalink|古墳時代|Q459939}}から{{jalink|平安時代|Q193292}}（{{jalink|4世紀|Q8099}}〜{{jalink|10世紀|Q8052}}）にわたる。中国・朝鮮半島製品を含む、各種の銅鏡、金銅（銅に金メッキ）製の馬具類のほか、土師器、三彩陶器、滑石製品、玉類、刀剣類などが出土品の主なものである。出土品中には{{jalink|ペルシャ}}・{{jalink|サーサーン朝|Q83891}}製と見られるガラス椀の破片などもある。考古学、美術史、宗教史、古代史など、さまざまな分野の研究に資するところの多い、学術的にきわめて貴重な資料である。3次にわたる発掘調査の結果は『沖ノ島』『続沖ノ島』『宗像沖ノ島』という報告書の形で刊行されている。これら出土品は宗像大社の神宝館で公開されている。{{jalink|1962年|Q2764}}に第1次・第2次発掘調査出土品が国宝に指定され、{{jalink|2003年|Q1986}}には第3次発掘調査出土品が追加指定されている。約8万点に及ぶ一括遺物の国宝としては、数量の上で日本一である。 === 重要文化財 === * 宗像神社辺津宮拝殿 * 宗像神社辺津宮本殿 * 木造狛犬一対 * 石造狛犬一対 * 藍韋威肩白胴丸 兜、壺袖付（あいかわおどしかたじろどうまる）-「{{jalink|胴丸|Q495328}}」は鎧の一種。 * 経石（正面{{jalink|阿弥陀如来|Q236242}}像・背面{{jalink|阿弥陀経|Q2661817}}）（阿弥陀仏経碑） * 宗像神社文書 12巻 附:宗像神社記録5巻、1冊、宗像社家文書惣目録 1冊 * 色定法師一筆一切経 4342巻1958年の重要文化財指定時の員数は4331巻であったが、1992年に11巻が追加指定された（平成4年6月22日文部省告示第85号）。 自文治三年（1187年）至嘉禄三年（1227年）奥書（宗像市田島 興聖寺所有、宗像大社管理） * 滑石製経筒 仁平4年銘（宗像市稲元区所有、宗像大社管理） === 史跡（国指定） === * 宗像神社境内 === 福岡県指定有形文化財 === * 宗像神社中津宮本殿 === その他 === * {{jalink|日本海海戦|Q208127}}で活躍した{{jalink|戦艦|Q182531}}{{jalink|三笠 (戦艦)|Q696891|三笠}}の羅針儀 * {{jalink|明応|Q1193841}}8年（{{jalink|1499年|Q6708}}）に鐘岬沖で浮上した翁面 === 宗像大社と出光佐三 === {{jalink|出光興産|Q2216770}}の創業者、{{jalink|出光佐三|Q7429431}}は旧{{jalink|宗像郡|Q6935606}}赤間宿の出身で、幼少より宗像大社を崇敬していた。1937年、邊津宮に参拝した折に神社の荒廃を嘆き、1942年に「宗像神社復興期成会」の結成を呼び掛け、初代会長に就任。戦中・戦後の活動停止を経て、1969年に宗像大社復興期成会に改組した{{Harvnb|公益財団法人出光美術館|2014|p=15}}。辺津宮本殿や拝殿の修復など佐三の寄進によるところが大きいが本人が畏れ多いと辞退したため境内にその名を示す痕跡は永く無かったが、現在は神宝館などに佐三を顕彰する展示が為されている。佐三をモデルにした小説『{{jalink|海賊とよばれた男|Q16046027}}』では、{{jalink|敗戦|Q11499267}}に際して社内に{{jalink|分祀}}{{jalink|勧請}}した宗像神社の三女神に{{jalink|日本|Q17}}と{{jalink|日本民族|Q16782073}}の加護を祈願する姿が描かれている。佐三は伊勢神宮は皇室の祖先、宗像大社は国民の祖先、という自らの考えを著書に記している。{{jalink|東京都|Q1490}}{{jalink|千代田区|Q214051}}にある{{jalink|出光美術館|Q3076590}}は佐三が収集した美術品を展示する美術館で{{Cite web|和書|url=https://idemitsu-museum.or.jp/about/outline/|title=出光美術館について|accessdate=2024-09-24|website=出光美術館ウェブサイト|publisher=公益財団法人出光美術館}}、宗像・沖ノ島展などの特別展を定期的に開催し、また毎年10月17日に宗像大社で献茶祭が行われる際には所蔵の名物茶道具が多く出され、{{jalink|表千家|Q3278052}}宗匠が献茶し、神社の永続と佐三翁を偲ぶ。 === 名物 === * 宗像大社せんべい * 幸福餅 === 交通 === バス利用の場合 * 辺津宮 - {{jalink|鹿児島本線|Q1187520}}・{{jalink|東郷駅|Q5359652}}から{{jalink|西鉄バス|Q11629843}}1番系統神湊波止場ゆきに乗車し、「宗像大社前」下車。所要時間10分。 * 中津宮・沖津宮遥拝所 - 鹿児島本線・東郷駅から西鉄バス神湊波止場ゆきに乗車し終点下車（所要時間20分）。{{jalink|神湊漁港}}より{{jalink|大島港 (福岡県)|Q30933915|大島港}}まで{{jalink|宗像市営渡船|Q11451853}}の旅客船で15分、フェリーで25分。大島港より中津宮まで徒歩5分（800メートル）。 マイカーの場合、{{jalink|九州自動車道|Q1060803}}{{jalink|若宮インターチェンジ|Q1575782}}から辺津宮まで16キロメートル、神湊漁港まで19キロメートル。もしくは同{{jalink|古賀インターチェンジ|Q1577981}}から辺津宮まで15キロメートル、神湊漁港まで17キロメートル。神湊漁港から宗像市営渡船で大島港に渡り、中津宮まで400メートル、沖津宮遥拝所まで2.3キロメートル。 === 関連書籍 === * 安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』神社新報社、1968年、59頁 * 白井永二・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』{{jalink|東京堂出版|Q11524645}}、1979年、327頁 * 上山春平他『日本「神社」総覧』{{jalink|新人物往来社|Q11501312}}、1992年、264-265頁 * 『神道の本』{{jalink|Gakken|Q86741099|学研}}、1992年、211頁 === 脚注 === {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} === 参考文献 === * 福岡市 編『ふくおか歴史散歩』（{{jalink|平野国臣|Q11483648}}が宗像大社の営繕を担当） * {{jalink|藤原新也|Q5157839}}・{{jalink|安部龍太郎|Q4721954}}『神の島　沖ノ島』（{{jalink|小学館|Q785697}} 2013年） * {{Cite book |和書| author = 公益財団法人出光美術館 | title = 宗像大社国宝展 神の島・沖ノ島と大社の神宝 | publisher = 公益財団法人出光美術館 | year = 2014 |ref = harv}} === 関連項目 === {{Commonscat}} * {{jalink|宗像神社|Q11451876}} * {{jalink|宗像三女神|Q10948069}} * {{jalink|鎮国寺|Q11651157}} - The former {{jalink|Shakaku|Q10444029}} was {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System #Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}. There are over 7,000 shrines throughout Japan, including {{jalink|Munakata Shrine|Q11451876}}, {{jalink|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763}}, and {{jalink|Munakata Three Goddess It is the headquarters of the shrine that enshrines |Q10948069}}, and in ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', it is referred to as ``''Doshu Taka''''. {{jalink|Okinoshima|Q7082047}} floating in the {{jalink|Genkai Sea|Q498047}} is considered a sacred area, and many of the {{jalink|ancient|Q41493}}{{jalink|rituals}} offerings excavated on Okinoshima have been designated as {{jalink|national treasure|Q1139795}}. It is also called ``Ura Ise''.It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in {{jalink|2017|Q25290}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}29) as one of the constituent assets of '''{{jalink|"Island inhabited by the Gods" Munakata/Okinoshima and Related Heritage Group|Q324638}}'''. === Overview === Munakata Taisha is a general term for three shrines: ``Okitsu-miya'' on {{jalink|Okinoshima|Q7082047}}, ``Nakatsu-miya'' on {{jalink|Chikuzen Oshima}}, and ``Hetsu-miya'' (Soja) on Tajima, {{jalink|Munakata City|Q819603}}, but nowadays it often refers to just ``Hetsu-miya''. Hetsu Shrine is enshrined in Tajima, Munakata City, and is also called ``Tajima-sama'' by the locals. There is also Okitsu-miya Yohaisho ('''Teitsu-miya'') on Chikuzen Oshima. On the map, Nakatsu-miya, which is 11 km away from Hetsu-miya, and Okitsu-miya, which is 49 km further away, are all in a straight line. It is one of the oldest shrines in Japan, whose history is recorded in the {{jalink|Kikiki|Q842308}}, and has been a maritime route for politics, economy, and culture between the continent and the peninsula since ancient times. Since ancient times, he has been worshiped for his divine power as a {{jalink|god|Q178885}} of {{jalink|sea surface|Q125465|sea}} and {{jalink|traffic safety|Q1147899}}, but now he is worshiped not only on the sea but also on all roads, land, and traffic safety under the name of Doshu Taka.{{jalink|faith|Q5410500}}. For this reason, many {{jalink|cars|Q1420}} with Munakata Taisha Shrine {{jalink|stickers|Q2872553|stickers}} can be seen in Fukuoka Prefecture and its surrounding areas, and there are also a large number of people who purchase a new car and receive a purification at the prayer hall. Additionally, the traffic safety charms that are worn on cars originate from Munakata Taisha Shrine.Okinoshima Island, where Okitsu-miya is located, is located at a key point for maritime traffic.Since ancient times, people have been called ``Oiwasama'' because people were not allowed to enter the island and reveal what they saw or heard, and the entire island is {{jalink|go|Q11488760}}{{jalink|divine body|Q327532}}. For this reason, even today {{jalink|women are prohibited|Q11446290}}, and even men must undergo {{jalink|misogi|Q1936265}} before landing. This is sometimes said to be gender discrimination, but there is a theory that the island's god is a female god ({{jalink|Tashin Himekami}}) and that women who land on the island are said to be jealous and have a curse, but this is not confirmed. Excavations on Okinoshima Island have been carried out for more than ten years since 1952, and a large amount of ritual artifacts (offerings) such as ancient ritual remains and ornaments from the 4th to 9th centuries were discovered, as well as stone tools, pottery, and other artifacts from the {{jalink|Jomon period|Q52824}} to the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}. For this reason, Okinoshima is commonly called the ``{{jalink|Shosoin|Q2379007}}'' of the sea, and it is remembered that it has been the subject of {{jalink|faith|Q5410500}} by {{jalink|Amajin|Q9495537}} and others since prehistoric times. Currently, it is designated as an emergency evacuation port during typhoons. The plaque of {{jalink|Divine Rescript|Q11588781}} that is hung in the shrine's worship hall is {{jalink|Calligraphy|Q11498466}} by {{jalink|Prince Fushiminomiya Sadaai|Q466326}}, and the plaque at Munakata Palace is the script of Imperial Envoy Shonii Gon Dainagon, Akitaka Hamuro.{{jalink|Egypt|Q79}}{{jalink|Archaeologist|Q3621491}} {{jalink|Sakuji Yoshimura|Q2740406}} advocated A movement arose to designate the ritual sites of Noshima and the Munakata region as {{jalink|World Heritage|Q9259}}, and in 2009, "Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, Hetsu-miya" and "Okitsu-miya Yohaisho" were established. It was added to the tentative list as a group of related heritage sites including the ``Island inhabited by the Gods,'' Munakata/Okinoshima, and was nominated in 2015, and in July 2017, it was officially registered as a World Heritage Site at the {{jalink|UNESCO}} World Heritage Committee meeting in {{jalink|Poland|Q36}} and {{jalink|Krakow|Q31487}}. === Enshrined God === Each of the three shrines enshrines the following gods, collectively known as {{jalink|Three Goddesses of Munakata|Q10948069}} (Munakata Okami). * Okitsuguu Shrine: {{jalink|Takiribime|Q10932870|Tashin Himekami}} * Nakatsugu Shrine: {{jalink|Tagitsuhime|Q10932592|Tanatsu Himekami}} * Hetsu Shrine: {{jalink|Ichikishima Hime|Q11059454|Ichikishima Himekami}} File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Hetsu Shrine).JPG|Hetsu Shrine Worship Hall (photo before the construction of the shrine) File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Nakatsu Shrine Worship Hall File:Munakata Taisha Okitsu Shrine.JPG|Okitsu Shrine Worship Hall === Shrine building === [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden1.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Worship Hall]] [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden2.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Hall of Worship]] [[File:Munakata-taisha shimboku.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Sacred Tree]] [[File:Munakata-taisha museum.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Shinpokan]] === Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya === * Main shrine (first shrine, Ichikishima Hime is the enshrined deity. Donated by the Kuroda clan, the lord of Fukuoka domain.) * Torii, et al. === History ===In {{jalink|tradition|Q36192}}, it has {{jalink|origin}} in {{jalink|Japanese mythology|Q814158}}. {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602}} and {{jalink|Susanoo|Q272993|Amaterasu and Susa}} During Noo's Pledge|Q11284880|Pledge}} (Pledge), Amaterasu Omikami bit down the Sword of Suho, and the three goddesses of Munakata were born from the fragments that blew out. The origin of Munakata Taisha Shrine is said to be that the goddesses worshiped Amaterasu's ``''{{jalink|divine edict|Q11588781}}'''' and descended to the islands of Tsukushi Munakata in the Genkai Sea in the Kaihoku region to protect and help the imperial descendant {{jalink|Ninigi no Mikoto}}, and came to rule over this land. The only ``gods who descended from heaven to earth'' mentioned in {{jalink|Kiki|Q842308}} are {{jalink|Ninigi no Mikoto}} and the three goddesses of Munakata who descended from heaven before {{jalink|Descent of Tenson|Q1084733}}. This is the oldest record of the Kiki in which the names of gods and their enshrined locations are clearly described. According to the {{jalink|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664}}{{jalink|Fudōki|Q1194534}} regarding the shrine worship of Munakata Sangu Shrine, ``Saikaido Fudoki says, ``Since the time of Saimon Mountain, where Munakata Okami and his god were descended, , Ao-tama-Okikutsu-miya-no-omote, eight-shaku-purple-purple-oki-Okitsu-miya-no-omote, Yata-kagami-Okibetsu-miya-no-omote, and these three tables are placed in the form of the god's body. There is an anecdote that says, ``Sannomiya, Soku-no-in, Gin-gata-gun, Gonin-kai, descendants of Munakata Ki-Okai-no-Mikoto, and now Munakata Ason, etc.'' In ``{{jalink|Kojiki|Q813031}}'', Munakata is given the character ``Musakata,'' and is also written ``Munetakata'' or ``Munakata,'' but there is also a theory that it was originally Mizugata. It has been worshiped as the guardian deity of the local people since ancient times, and it is said that when {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803}} prayed for safe voyages during her {{jalink|Sankan Conquest|Q11249435}}, she had a miraculous experience here, and it is said that she had a habit of sending envoys to Munakata whenever the situation arises. It was valued by the {{jalink|Yamato Imperial Court}}, and since ancient times, whenever the capital was transferred, a spirit of our company was enshrined in the {{jalink|kendokoro|Q11635085}} (kashikodokoro) of the imperial court. This anecdote also reveals how he came to be worshiped as a {{jalink|guardian|Q131278957}} of safe navigation.With the introduction of {{jalink|ritsuryo system#Japanese ritsuryo system|Q742460|ritsuryo system}}, {{jalink|kokugunri system|Q11421491|kokugun system}}, {{jalink|Munakata county|Q6935606|one county of Munakata}} was given as {{jalink|Temple territory|Q11458058|Shinryo}}, The local {{jalink|gozoku|Q84066}}{{jalink|Munakata clan|Q16481907|Munegata clan}} served the shrine as {{jalink|Shinto priest|Q60523|Shinto priest}}, and also took charge of the {{jalink|administration|Q31728}} of {{jalink|Kamigun|Q11590937}}. According to the {{jalink|stone monument|Q178743}} that records the origins of the Munakata clan, the head of the Munakata clan has welcomed the daughter of a Chinese {{jalink|merchant|Q215536}} as his {{jalink|lawful wife|Q1765533}} for two generations. Also, {{jalink|Munegata Tokuzen|Q11451927}} put his daughter {{jalink|Amago Musume|Q11464914}} into the {{jalink|Inner Palace|Q5353683}} of {{jalink|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181}}, and {{jalink|Hakuji|Q540118}} for 5 years ({ The first prince, {{jalink|Prince Takaichi|Q837590}}, who was born to the two in {{jalink|654|Q31109}}, achieved great success by helping his father in the {{jalink|Jinshin War|Q2378252}}, and was later appointed as {{jalink|Dajodaijin|Q1157586}}. {{jalink|King Nagaya|Q1963492}} was the son of Takaichi and also the ancestor of the {{jalink|Takashina clan|Q11673216}}. In {{jalink|807|Q30016}} ({{jalink|Daido (Japan)|Q1373191|Daido}}2), 74 houses were donated, {{jalink|840|Q29936}} ({{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jōwa}} 7th year), he was conferred {{jalink|Junior Fifth Rank Lower}}, and then became {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōgan}} first year) and {{jalink|Senior Second Rank|Q11123277}}. In the 4th year of {{jalink|Tenkei|Q1327340}} (after the {{jalink|Tenkei War|Q11442602}}), advance further and obtain {{jalink|Shinkai|Q11591025}} of {{jalink|Shoichii|Q11123258}}. {{jalink|979|Q23784}} ({{jalink|Tengen (Japan)|Q1327101|Tengen}}2 years) The {{jalink|Grand Shrine}} position is established by {{jalink|Dajokan|Q1192939}}.After the {{jalink|Kamakura period|Q236205}}, the {{jalink|Munakata clan|Q16481907}}, who was the descendant of the Munakata clan and inherited the position of the Daiguji family, became samurai and grew into a powerful kokujin feudal lord, but during the Sengoku period, {{jalink|Ouchi clan|Q1348 909}}, {{jalink|Otomo clan|Q1096662}}, {{jalink|Shoni clan|Q2975368}}, and other nearby feudal lords were mobilized for wars, and Munakata Taisha Shrine also became the target of military attacks and was frequently arsoned and destroyed, and the Munakata clan also declined. However, each time it was worshiped by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} and {{jalink|Samurai|Q2927809}} and was repeatedly rebuilt. The current Hetsu Shrine {{jalink|main hall|Q2044994}}, with its beautiful large shingled roof, was rebuilt by the chief priest {{jalink|Ujisada Munakata|Q10204112}} in the 6th year of Tensho ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}). Ken, Hetsu-miya {{jalink|haiden|Q3125745}} was rebuilt in Tensho 16 ({{jalink|1590|Q6764}}) by {{jalink|Takakage Kobayakawa|Q1143508}}, the lord of Chikuzen. Both the main hall of worship of Hetsu Shrine are designated as national {{jalink|Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622}}. The rituals carried out by the Munakata clan were then passed on to the {{jalink|Kusakari clan}} ({{jalink|Shigetsugu Kusakari|Q22126274}}). During the Edo period, it is often reported that the {{jalink|Chikuzen|Q242409}}{{jalink|Fukuoka Domain|Q208766}} lord {{jalink|Kuroda clan|Q2975305}} constructed and repaired shrine buildings, and {{jalink|donated|Q11455717}} the shrine's territory. After that, from the end of the Edo period to the Meiji period ({{jalink|Haibutsu Kishaku|Q702298}}, Byobuyama {{jalink|Chinkokuji|Q11651157}}, which was {{jalink|Jinguji|Q1074971}}, was separated from the Taisha shrine.Also, in {{jalink|1871|Q7746}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}4), it was listed as ``Munakata Shrine'' in {{jalink|Kokuheichusha}} in the {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. On April 22 of the following year, he was promoted to {{jalink|Kanpei Chusha}}. Then, on July 11, {{jalink|1901|Q2035}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}34), it was promoted to the highest rank, {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}. After {{jalink|Showa|Q327567}} {{jalink|World War II|Q362}}, the shrine grounds were in ruins. Born in Akama (Akama district, Munakata city), he has worshiped Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. It was built with a donation from {{jalink|Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431}}, a businessman whom he admired, and he worked hard to encourage the government to investigate and excavate the Okinoshima ritual ruins where Okitsu Shrine is located. === Kei Yukiyuki === {{jalink|1983|Q2434}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}58), Crown Prince Akihito (later {{jalink|Emperor Empress Akihito||Retired Emperor Akihito}}) and his wife Michiko (later {{jalink|Emperor Empress Michiko|Q87610}}) visited Hetsu Shrine. {{jalink|2013|Q1998}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}25), {{jalink|Naruhito|Q217096|Crown Prince Naruhito}} visited Hetsu Shrine. {{jalink|2017|Q25290}} (2017) {{jalink|October 29|Q2951}}, Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko became the first emperors and empresses in history to visit Hetsu Shrine to pay their respects.{{Cite news|Japanese book|title=Fukuoka) Their Majesties visit Munakata Taisha, a World Heritage Site: Asahi Shimbun Digital|url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASKBY5R38KBYTIPE012.html|accessdate=2018-05-08|language=ja-JP|work=Asahi Shimbun Digital}}{{Broken link|date=March 2024}}. In addition, as a member of the imperial family, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}}'s younger brother {{jalink|archaeologist|Q3621491}} {{jalink|Prince Takahito Mikasa|Q280229}} visited the shrine many times, and he also composed waka poems about Okinoshima. === Sessha === * Kamiminato Munakata Shrine (Old Shrine) - Outside the precincts of the shrine (Autumn Grand Festival Tajima Hojokai, {{jalink|Miare Festival|Q11278738}}, where mikoshi of the three goddesses are lined up and dedicated) === Shinto rituals and festivals === * New Year's Festival - Shinto rituals to celebrate the New Year, such as Saidan Festival. 1st to 3rd of New Year every year. * Spring Festival - April 1st-3rd every year. * Summer Purification - Held at the end of July every year. * {{jalink|Tanabata|Q13423122}} Festival - Held every year on {{jalink|lunar calendar|Q11511066}} at the evening of July 7th at the Nakatsu Shrine of {{jalink|Chikuzen Oshima}}. There are {{jalink|Kengyu}}sha and {{jalink|Orijo}}sha, in front of which bamboo bamboo leaves with strips of paper are erected to pray for improvement in the craft. A ritual is held to predict the fate of men and women by looking at their reflections in the water, and a Tanabata {{jalink|calligraphy|Q11498466}} competition is also held. According to the Shohei Annual Events, it is {{jalink|1346|Q6080}} ``Tanabata Mushifuri Shinto ritual on the seventh day of July''. * Autumn Festival - October 1st to 3rd every year. Prior to the event at Hetsu Shrine's main shrine on the 1st to 3rd, there is a {{jalink|divine welcome}} ritual held at Nakatsu-miya and Okitsu-miya shrines, and a {{jalink|divine celebration||marine divine celebration}} is held with colorful flags and banners set up by fishing boats (Miare Festival). At the main shrine, {{jalink|Okina|Q11610439}} dances, customary dances, {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}}, dedication {{jalink|sumo|Q40561}}, etc. are performed. Its origins date back to the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, and its official name is ``Tajima Hojokai.'' * Kencha Festival - Held on October 17th every year. * Harvest Festival - A new festival that began to be held every year after the Heisei Emperor and Empress paid their respects to our company.* West Japan Chrysanthemum Exhibition - A chrysanthemum exhibition held every November. A large number of cultivated chrysanthemums from Kyushu and other prefectures in western Japan will be on display and appreciated. * Ancient Ceremony Festival, Hibisai Festival - A secret winter festival with a history of over 800 years that is held in mid-December every year. * New Year's Purification - New Year's Eve Shinto ritual held on New Year's Eve every year. === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * '''Items excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture/Traditional Items excavated from the Oki-tsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture'''' Bulk: A collection of artifacts excavated from over 20 ritual sites on Okinoshima, a remote island in the Genkai Sea. It was excavated during the first to third excavations from {{jalink|1954|Q18581}} to {{jalink|1971|Q2475}}. Spreads from {{jalink|Kofun period|Q459939}} to {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}} ({{jalink|4th century|Q8099}} to {{jalink|10th century|Q8052}}). The main artifacts excavated include various bronze mirrors, horse harnesses made of gilt bronze (gold plated on copper), including products from China and the Korean Peninsula, as well as Haji ware, Sansai pottery, talcum products, jade items, and swords. Among the excavated items are fragments of glass bowls thought to have been made by {{jalink|Persia}} and {{jalink|Sassanid|Q83891}}. It is an extremely valuable academic resource that contributes to research in a variety of fields, including archaeology, art history, religious history, and ancient history. The results of three excavations have been published in the form of reports called ``Okinoshima,'' ``Zoku Okinoshima,'' and ``Munakata Okinoshima.'' These excavated items are on display at the sacred treasure museum of Munakata Taisha Shrine. In {{jalink|1962|Q2764}}, the artifacts from the first and second excavations were designated as national treasures, and in {{jalink|2003|Q1986}}, the artifacts from the third excavation were additionally designated as national treasures. It is the largest national treasure in Japan in terms of quantity, consisting of approximately 80,000 relics. After adding undesignated cultural properties to this list, they were designated as national treasures as ``Artifacts excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine, Fukuoka Prefecture; (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 75 of 2006)
=== Important cultural property === * Munakata Shrine Hetsumiya Worship Hall * Munakata Shrine Hetsumiya Main Hall * A pair of wooden guardian dogs * A pair of stone guardian dogs * Aikawa Odoka Tajiro Doumaru with helmet and pot sleeves - "{{jalink|Doumaru|Q495328}}" is a type of armor. * Sutra stone (Front {{jalink|Amida Tathagata|Q236242}} statue, back {{jalink|Amida Sutra|Q2661817}}) (Amida Buddha sutra monument) * Munakata Shrine Documents Volume 12 with attached: Munakata Shrine Records Volume 5, 1 volume, Munakata Shrine Documents Somokuroki 1 volume * 4,342 volumes of Shirojoboshi's Isshu Issukyo When it was designated as an important cultural property in 1958, there were 4,331 volumes, but 11 volumes were additionally designated in 1992 (Ministry of Education Notification No. 85, June 22, 1992). Colophon from 1187 to 1227 (Owned by Koshoji Temple, Tajima, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) * Talcstone sutra cylinder inscribed in the 4th year of the Ninpei era (owned by Inamoto Ward, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) === Historic Site (Nationally Designated) === * Munakata Shrine grounds === Fukuoka Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === * Munakata Shrine Nakatsumiya Main Hall === Others === * Compass of {{jalink|Battleship|Q182531}}{{jalink|Mikasa (battleship)|Q696891|Mikasa}}, which was active in {{jalink|Battle of the Sea of Japan|Q208127}} * An Okina mask surfaced off the coast of Cape Kane in {{jalink|Meio|Q1193841}}8 ({{jalink|1499|Q6708}}) === Munakata Taisha and Sazo Idemitsu ==={{jalink|Idemitsu Kosan|Q2216770}}'s founder, {{jalink|Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431}}, is from the former {{jalink|Munakata District|Q6935606}} Akama-juku, and has revered Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. In 1937, when he visited Betsu Shrine, he lamented the devastation of the shrine, and in 1942 he called for the formation of the ``Munakata Shrine Restoration Society'' and became its first president. After suspending its activities during and after the war, it was reorganized as the Munakata Taisha Reconstruction Society in 1969. The restoration of the main shrine and worship hall of Hetsu Shrine was largely due to Sazo's donations, but as he declined out of fear, there were no traces of his name within the shrine grounds for a long time, but there are now exhibits honoring Sazo at Shinpokan and other places. In the novel "{{jalink|A Man Called a Pirate|Q16046027}}," which is based on Sazo, upon {{jalink|defeat|Q11499267}}, a separate shrine was established within the company. }}It is depicted praying to the three goddesses of Munakata Shrine, who have been praying for the protection of {{jalink|Japan|Q17}} and the {{jalink|Japanese people|Q16782073}}. Sazo wrote in his book that he believed that Ise Shrine was the ancestor of the imperial family, and Munakata Taisha Shrine was the ancestor of the people. {{jalink|Tokyo|Q1490}}{{jalink|Idemitsu Art Museum|Q3076590}} located in {{jalink|Chiyoda-ku|Q214051}} is an art museum that exhibits artworks collected by Sazo.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://idemitsu-museum.or.jp/about/outline/|title=About Idemitsu Museum of Art|accessdate=2024-09-24|website=Idemitsu Museum of Art website|publisher=Public The Idemitsu Museum of Art}} regularly holds special exhibitions such as the Munakata/Okinoshima Exhibition, and on October 17th every year, when the tea ceremony is held at Munakata Taisha Shrine, many of the famous tea utensils from the collection are put on display, and the {{jalink|Omotesenke|Q3278052}} master offers tea, commemorating the perpetuation of the shrine and remembering Sazo. === Specialty === * Munakata Taisha Shrine rice crackers * Happiness Mochi === Transportation === By bus * Hetsunomiya - From {{jalink|Kagoshima Main Line|Q1187520}}/{{jalink|Togo Station|Q5359652}}, take {{jalink|Nishitetsu Bus|Q11629843}} Route 1 bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at "Munakata Taisha-mae". It takes 10 minutes. * Nakatsumiya/Okitsumiya Yohaisho - From Togo Station on the Kagoshima Main Line, take the Nishitetsu bus bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at the last stop (20 minutes). From {{jalink|Kamiminato Fishing Port}} to {{jalink|Oshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|Q30933915|Oshima Port}}, it takes 15 minutes by the {{jalink|Munakata Municipal Ferry|Q11451853}} passenger ship, or 25 minutes by ferry. 5 minutes walk (800 meters) from Oshima Port to Nakatsunomiya. If you have your own car, it is 16 kilometers from {{jalink|Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803}}{{jalink|Wakamiya Interchange|Q1575782}} to Hetsunomiya and 19 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. Alternatively, from the same {{jalink|Koga Interchange|Q1577981}}, it is 15 kilometers to Hetsunomiya and 17 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. From Kamiminato Fishing Port, take the Munakata Municipal Ferry to Oshima Port, 400 meters to Nakatsu-miya Shrine, and 2.3 kilometers to Okitsu-miya Yohaisho. === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 59 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{jalink|Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645}}, 1979, 327 pages * Shunpei Ueyama et al., “Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines” {{jalink|Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312}}, 1992, pp. 264-265 * "Book of Shinto" {{jalink|Gakken|Q86741099|Gakken}}, 1992, p. 211 === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === References === * "Fukuoka History Walk" edited by Fukuoka City ({{jalink|Kuniomi Hirano|Q11483648}} was in charge of the maintenance of Munakata Taisha Shrine) * {{jalink|Shinya Fujiwara|Q5157839}}・{{jalink|Ryuutaro Abe|Q4721954}} "Okinoshima, the Island of the Gods" ({{jalink|Shogakukan|Q785697}} 2013) * {{Cite book |Japanese book| author = Idemitsu Museum of Art | title = Munakata Taisha National Treasure Exhibition: The Island of the Gods, Okinoshima and the sacred treasures of the shrine | publisher = Idemitsu Museum of Art, public interest incorporated foundation | year = 2014 |ref = harv}} === Related items === {{Commonscat}} * {{jalink|Munakata Shrine|Q11451876}} * {{jalink|Three goddesses of Munakata|Q10948069}} * {{jalink|Chinkokuji|Q11651157}} - Former Munakata Taisha Jinguji * {{jalink|Nibaru-Nuyama Tumulus Group|Q22119078}} - Said to be the burial place of the ancient Munakata clan * {{jalink|List of Munakata Daiguji|Q11451851}} * {{jalink|List of historical sites in Kyushu and Okinawa region|Q11370155}} * {{jalink|Munakata/Okinoshima and related heritage sites}} * {{jalink|Umi no Michi Munakatakan|Q38277686}} === External link === * [https://munakata-taisha.or.jp/ Munakata Taisha Official Homepage] ** {{Instagram|munakata_taisha}} ** {{Facebook|munakata.taisha.official}} * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/862 Articles excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine, Fukuoka Prefecture] - The former {{jalink|Shakaku|Q10444029}} was {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System #Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}. There are over 7,000 shrines throughout Japan, including {{jalink|Munakata Shrine|Q11451876}}, {{jalink|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763}}, and {{jalink|Munakata Three Goddess It is the headquarters of the shrine that enshrines |Q10948069}}, and in ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', it is referred to as ``''Doshu Taka''''. {{jalink|Okinoshima|Q7082047}} floating in the {{jalink|Genkai Sea|Q498047}} is considered a sacred area, and many of the {{jalink|ancient|Q41493}}{{jalink|rituals}} offerings excavated on Okinoshima have been designated as {{jalink|national treasure|Q1139795}}. It is also called ``Ura Ise''.It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in {{jalink|2017|Q25290}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}29) as one of the constituent assets of '''{{jalink|"Island inhabited by the Gods" Munakata/Okinoshima and Related Heritage Group|Q324638}}'''. === Overview === Munakata Taisha is a general term for three shrines: ``Okitsu-miya'' on {{jalink|Okinoshima|Q7082047}}, ``Nakatsu-miya'' on {{jalink|Chikuzen Oshima}}, and ``Hetsu-miya'' (Soja) on Tajima, {{jalink|Munakata City|Q819603}}, but nowadays it often refers to just ``Hetsu-miya''. Hetsu Shrine is enshrined in Tajima, Munakata City, and is also called ``Tajima-sama'' by the locals. There is also Okitsu-miya Yohaisho ('''Teitsu-miya'') on Chikuzen Oshima. On the map, Nakatsu-miya, which is 11 km away from Hetsu-miya, and Okitsu-miya, which is 49 km further away, are all in a straight line. It is one of the oldest shrines in Japan, whose history is recorded in the {{jalink|Kikiki|Q842308}}, and has been a maritime route for politics, economy, and culture between the continent and the peninsula since ancient times. Since ancient times, he has been worshiped for his divine power as a {{jalink|god|Q178885}} of {{jalink|sea surface|Q125465|sea}} and {{jalink|traffic safety|Q1147899}}, but now he is worshiped not only on the sea but also on all roads, land, and traffic safety under the name of Doshu Taka.{{jalink|faith|Q5410500}}. For this reason, many {{jalink|cars|Q1420}} with Munakata Taisha Shrine {{jalink|stickers|Q2872553|stickers}} can be seen in Fukuoka Prefecture and its surrounding areas, and there are also a large number of people who purchase a new car and receive a purification at the prayer hall. Additionally, the traffic safety charms that are worn on cars originate from Munakata Taisha Shrine.Okinoshima Island, where Okitsu-miya is located, is located at a key point for maritime traffic.Since ancient times, people have been called ``Oiwasama'' because people were not allowed to enter the island and reveal what they saw or heard, and the entire island is {{jalink|go|Q11488760}}{{jalink|divine body|Q327532}}. For this reason, even today {{jalink|women are prohibited|Q11446290}}, and even men must undergo {{jalink|misogi|Q1936265}} before landing. This is sometimes said to be gender discrimination, but there is a theory that the island's god is a female god ({{jalink|Tashin Himekami}}) and that women who land on the island are said to be jealous and have a curse, but this is not confirmed. Excavations on Okinoshima Island have been carried out for more than ten years since 1952, and a large amount of ritual artifacts (offerings) such as ancient ritual remains and ornaments from the 4th to 9th centuries were discovered, as well as stone tools, pottery, and other artifacts from the {{jalink|Jomon period|Q52824}} to the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}. For this reason, Okinoshima is commonly called the ``{{jalink|Shosoin|Q2379007}}'' of the sea, and it is remembered that it has been the subject of {{jalink|faith|Q5410500}} by {{jalink|Amajin|Q9495537}} and others since prehistoric times. Currently, it is designated as an emergency evacuation port during typhoons. The plaque of {{jalink|Divine Rescript|Q11588781}} that is hung in the shrine's worship hall is {{jalink|Calligraphy|Q11498466}} by {{jalink|Prince Fushiminomiya Sadaai|Q466326}}, and the plaque at Munakata Palace is the script of Imperial Envoy Shonii Gon Dainagon, Akitaka Hamuro.{{jalink|Egypt|Q79}}{{jalink|Archaeologist|Q3621491}} {{jalink|Sakuji Yoshimura|Q2740406}} advocated A movement arose to designate the ritual sites of Noshima and the Munakata region as {{jalink|World Heritage|Q9259}}, and in 2009, "Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, Hetsu-miya" and "Okitsu-miya Yohaisho" were established. It was added to the tentative list as a group of related heritage sites including the ``Island inhabited by the Gods,'' Munakata/Okinoshima, and was nominated in 2015, and in July 2017, it was officially registered as a World Heritage Site at the {{jalink|UNESCO}} World Heritage Committee meeting in {{jalink|Poland|Q36}} and {{jalink|Krakow|Q31487}}. === Enshrined God === Each of the three shrines enshrines the following gods, collectively known as {{jalink|Three Goddesses of Munakata|Q10948069}} (Munakata Okami). * Okitsuguu Shrine: {{jalink|Takiribime|Q10932870|Tashin Himekami}} * Nakatsugu Shrine: {{jalink|Tagitsuhime|Q10932592|Tanatsu Himekami}} * Hetsu Shrine: {{jalink|Ichikishima Hime|Q11059454|Ichikishima Himekami}} File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Hetsu Shrine).JPG|Hetsu Shrine Worship Hall (photo before the construction of the shrine) File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Nakatsu Shrine Worship Hall File:Munakata Taisha Okitsu Shrine.JPG|Okitsu Shrine Worship Hall === Shrine building === [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden1.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Worship Hall]] [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden2.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Hall of Worship]] [[File:Munakata-taisha shimboku.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Sacred Tree]] [[File:Munakata-taisha museum.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Shinpokan]] === Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya === * Main shrine (first shrine, Ichikishima Hime is the enshrined deity. Donated by the Kuroda clan, the lord of Fukuoka domain.) * Torii, et al. === History ===In {{jalink|tradition|Q36192}}, it has {{jalink|origin}} in {{jalink|Japanese mythology|Q814158}}. {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602}} and {{jalink|Susanoo|Q272993|Amaterasu and Susa}} During Noo's Pledge|Q11284880|Pledge}} (Pledge), Amaterasu Omikami bit down the Sword of Suho, and the three goddesses of Munakata were born from the fragments that blew out. The origin of Munakata Taisha Shrine is said to be that the goddesses worshiped Amaterasu's ``''{{jalink|divine edict|Q11588781}}'''' and descended to the islands of Tsukushi Munakata in the Genkai Sea in the Kaihoku region to protect and help the imperial descendant {{jalink|Ninigi no Mikoto}}, and came to rule over this land. The only ``gods who descended from heaven to earth'' mentioned in {{jalink|Kiki|Q842308}} are {{jalink|Ninigi no Mikoto}} and the three goddesses of Munakata who descended from heaven before {{jalink|Descent of Tenson|Q1084733}}. This is the oldest record of the Kiki in which the names of gods and their enshrined locations are clearly described. According to the {{jalink|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664}}{{jalink|Fudōki|Q1194534}} regarding the shrine worship of Munakata Sangu Shrine, ``Saikaido Fudoki says, ``Since the time of Saimon Mountain, where Munakata Okami and his god were descended, , Ao-tama-Okikutsu-miya-no-omote, eight-shaku-purple-purple-oki-Okitsu-miya-no-omote, Yata-kagami-Okibetsu-miya-no-omote, and these three tables are placed in the form of the god's body. There is an anecdote that says, ``Sannomiya, Soku-no-in, Gin-gata-gun, Gonin-kai, descendants of Munakata Ki-Okai-no-Mikoto, and now Munakata Ason, etc.'' In ``{{jalink|Kojiki|Q813031}}'', Munakata is given the character ``Musakata,'' and is also written ``Munetakata'' or ``Munakata,'' but there is also a theory that it was originally Mizugata. It has been worshiped as the guardian deity of the local people since ancient times, and it is said that when {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803}} prayed for safe voyages during her {{jalink|Sankan Conquest|Q11249435}}, she had a miraculous experience here, and it is said that she had a habit of sending envoys to Munakata whenever the situation arises. It was valued by the {{jalink|Yamato Imperial Court}}, and since ancient times, whenever the capital was transferred, a spirit of our company was enshrined in the {{jalink|kendokoro|Q11635085}} (kashikodokoro) of the imperial court. This anecdote also reveals how he came to be worshiped as a {{jalink|guardian|Q131278957}} of safe navigation.With the introduction of {{jalink|ritsuryo system#Japanese ritsuryo system|Q742460|ritsuryo system}}, {{jalink|kokugunri system|Q11421491|kokugun system}}, {{jalink|Munakata county|Q6935606|one county of Munakata}} was given as {{jalink|Temple territory|Q11458058|Shinryo}}, The local {{jalink|gozoku|Q84066}}{{jalink|Munakata clan|Q16481907|Munegata clan}} served the shrine as {{jalink|Shinto priest|Q60523|Shinto priest}}, and also took charge of the {{jalink|administration|Q31728}} of {{jalink|Kamigun|Q11590937}}. According to the {{jalink|stone monument|Q178743}} that records the origins of the Munakata clan, the head of the Munakata clan has welcomed the daughter of a Chinese {{jalink|merchant|Q215536}} as his {{jalink|lawful wife|Q1765533}} for two generations. Also, {{jalink|Munegata Tokuzen|Q11451927}} put his daughter {{jalink|Amago Musume|Q11464914}} into the {{jalink|Inner Palace|Q5353683}} of {{jalink|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181}}, and {{jalink|Hakuji|Q540118}} for 5 years ({ The first prince, {{jalink|Prince Takaichi|Q837590}}, who was born to the two in {{jalink|654|Q31109}}, achieved great success by helping his father in the {{jalink|Jinshin War|Q2378252}}, and was later appointed as {{jalink|Dajodaijin|Q1157586}}. {{jalink|King Nagaya|Q1963492}} was the son of Takaichi and also the ancestor of the {{jalink|Takashina clan|Q11673216}}. In {{jalink|807|Q30016}} ({{jalink|Daido (Japan)|Q1373191|Daido}}2), 74 houses were donated, {{jalink|840|Q29936}} ({{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jōwa}} 7th year), he was conferred {{jalink|Junior Fifth Rank Lower}}, and then became {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōgan}} first year) and {{jalink|Senior Second Rank|Q11123277}}. In the 4th year of {{jalink|Tenkei|Q1327340}} (after the {{jalink|Tenkei War|Q11442602}}), advance further and obtain {{jalink|Shinkai|Q11591025}} of {{jalink|Shoichii|Q11123258}}. {{jalink|979|Q23784}} ({{jalink|Tengen (Japan)|Q1327101|Tengen}}2 years) The {{jalink|Grand Shrine}} position is established by {{jalink|Dajokan|Q1192939}}.After the {{jalink|Kamakura period|Q236205}}, the {{jalink|Munakata clan|Q16481907}}, who was the descendant of the Munakata clan and inherited the position of the Daiguji family, became samurai and grew into a powerful kokujin feudal lord, but during the Sengoku period, {{jalink|Ouchi clan|Q1348 909}}, {{jalink|Otomo clan|Q1096662}}, {{jalink|Shoni clan|Q2975368}}, and other nearby feudal lords were mobilized for wars, and Munakata Taisha Shrine also became the target of military attacks and was frequently arsoned and destroyed, and the Munakata clan also declined. However, each time it was worshiped by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} and {{jalink|Samurai|Q2927809}} and was repeatedly rebuilt. The current Hetsu Shrine {{jalink|main hall|Q2044994}}, with its beautiful large shingled roof, was rebuilt by the chief priest {{jalink|Ujisada Munakata|Q10204112}} in the 6th year of Tensho ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}). Ken, Hetsu-miya {{jalink|haiden|Q3125745}} was rebuilt in Tensho 16 ({{jalink|1590|Q6764}}) by {{jalink|Takakage Kobayakawa|Q1143508}}, the lord of Chikuzen. Both the main hall of worship of Hetsu Shrine are designated as national {{jalink|Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622}}. The rituals carried out by the Munakata clan were then passed on to the {{jalink|Kusakari clan}} ({{jalink|Shigetsugu Kusakari|Q22126274}}). During the Edo period, it is often reported that the {{jalink|Chikuzen|Q242409}}{{jalink|Fukuoka Domain|Q208766}} lord {{jalink|Kuroda clan|Q2975305}} constructed and repaired shrine buildings, and {{jalink|donated|Q11455717}} the shrine's territory. After that, from the end of the Edo period to the Meiji period ({{jalink|Haibutsu Kishaku|Q702298}}, Byobuyama {{jalink|Chinkokuji|Q11651157}}, which was {{jalink|Jinguji|Q1074971}}, was separated from the Taisha shrine.Also, in {{jalink|1871|Q7746}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}4), it was listed as ``Munakata Shrine'' in {{jalink|Kokuheichusha}} in the {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. After {{jalink|Showa|Q327567}} {{jalink|World War II|Q362}}, the shrine grounds were in ruins. Born in Akama (Akama district, Munakata city), he has worshiped Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. It was built with a donation from {{jalink|Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431}}, a businessman whom he admired, and he worked hard to encourage the government to investigate and excavate the Okinoshima ritual ruins where Okitsu Shrine is located. === Kei Yukiyuki === {{jalink|1983|Q2434}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}58), Crown Prince Akihito (later {{jalink|Emperor Empress Akihito||Retired Emperor Akihito}}) and his wife Michiko (later {{jalink|Emperor Empress Michiko|Q87610}}) visited Hetsu Shrine. {{jalink|2013|Q1998}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}25), {{jalink|Naruhito|Q217096|Crown Prince Naruhito}} visited Hetsu Shrine. {{jalink|2017|Q25290}} (2017) {{jalink|October 29|Q2951}}, Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko became the first emperors and empresses in history to visit Hetsu Shrine to pay their respects.{{Cite news|Japanese book|title=Fukuoka) Their Majesties visit Munakata Taisha, a World Heritage Site: Asahi Shimbun Digital|url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASKBY5R38KBYTIPE012.html|accessdate=2018-05-08|language=ja-JP|work=Asahi Shimbun Digital}}{{Broken link|date=March 2024}}. In addition, as a member of the imperial family, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}}'s younger brother {{jalink|archaeologist|Q3621491}} {{jalink|Prince Takahito Mikasa|Q280229}} visited the shrine many times, and he also composed waka poems about Okinoshima. === Sessha === * Kamiminato Munakata Shrine (Old Shrine) - Outside the precincts of the shrine (Autumn Grand Festival Tajima Hojokai, {{jalink|Miare Festival|Q11278738}}, where mikoshi of the three goddesses are lined up and dedicated) === Shinto rituals and festivals === * New Year's Festival - Shinto rituals to celebrate the New Year, such as Saidan Festival. 1st to 3rd of New Year every year. * Spring Festival - April 1st-3rd every year. * Summer Purification - Held at the end of July every year. * {{jalink|Tanabata|Q13423122}} Festival - Held every year on {{jalink|lunar calendar|Q11511066}} at the evening of July 7th at the Nakatsu Shrine of {{jalink|Chikuzen Oshima}}. There are {{jalink|Kengyu}}sha and {{jalink|Orijo}}sha, in front of which bamboo bamboo leaves with strips of paper are erected to pray for improvement in the craft. A ritual is held to predict the fate of men and women by looking at their reflections in the water, and a Tanabata {{jalink|calligraphy|Q11498466}} competition is also held. According to the Shohei Annual Events, it is {{jalink|1346|Q6080}} ``Tanabata Mushifuri Shinto ritual on the seventh day of July''. * Autumn Festival - October 1st to 3rd every year. Prior to the event at Hetsu Shrine's main shrine on the 1st to 3rd, there is a {{jalink|divine welcome}} ritual held at Nakatsu-miya and Okitsu-miya shrines, and a {{jalink|divine celebration||marine divine celebration}} is held with colorful flags and banners set up by fishing boats (Miare Festival). At the main shrine, {{jalink|Okina|Q11610439}} dances, customary dances, {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}}, dedication {{jalink|sumo|Q40561}}, etc. are performed. Its origins date back to the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, and its official name is ``Tajima Hojokai.'' * Kencha Festival - Held on October 17th every year. * Harvest Festival - A new festival that began to be held every year after the Heisei Emperor and Empress paid their respects to our company.* West Japan Chrysanthemum Exhibition - A chrysanthemum exhibition held every November. A large number of cultivated chrysanthemums from Kyushu and other prefectures in western Japan will be on display and appreciated. * Ancient Ceremony Festival, Hibisai Festival - A secret winter festival with a history of over 800 years that is held in mid-December every year. * New Year's Purification - New Year's Eve Shinto ritual held on New Year's Eve every year. === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * '''Items excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture/Traditional Items excavated from the Oki-tsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture'''' Bulk: A collection of artifacts excavated from over 20 ritual sites on Okinoshima, a remote island in the Genkai Sea. It was excavated during the first to third excavations from {{jalink|1954|Q18581}} to {{jalink|1971|Q2475}}. Spreads from {{jalink|Kofun period|Q459939}} to {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}} ({{jalink|4th century|Q8099}} to {{jalink|10th century|Q8052}}). The main artifacts excavated include various bronze mirrors, horse harnesses made of gilt bronze (gold plated on copper), including products from China and the Korean Peninsula, as well as Haji ware, Sansai pottery, talcum products, jade items, and swords. Among the excavated items are fragments of glass bowls thought to have been made by {{jalink|Persia}} and {{jalink|Sassanid|Q83891}}. It is an extremely valuable academic resource that contributes to research in a variety of fields, including archaeology, art history, religious history, and ancient history. The results of three excavations have been published in the form of reports called ``Okinoshima,'' ``Zoku Okinoshima,'' and ``Munakata Okinoshima.'' These excavated items are on display at the sacred treasure museum of Munakata Taisha Shrine. In {{jalink|1962|Q2764}}, the artifacts from the first and second excavations were designated as national treasures, and in {{jalink|2003|Q1986}}, the artifacts from the third excavation were additionally designated as national treasures. It is the largest national treasure in Japan in terms of quantity, consisting of approximately 80,000 relics. In 1937, when he visited Betsu Shrine, he lamented the devastation of the shrine, and in 1942 he called for the formation of the ``Munakata Shrine Restoration Society'' and became its first president. After suspending its activities during and after the war, it was reorganized as the Munakata Taisha Reconstruction Society in 1969. The restoration of the main shrine and worship hall of Hetsu Shrine was largely due to Sazo's donations, but as he declined out of fear, there were no traces of his name within the shrine grounds for a long time, but there are now exhibits honoring Sazo at Shinpokan and other places. In the novel "{{jalink|A Man Called a Pirate|Q16046027}}," which is based on Sazo, upon {{jalink|defeat|Q11499267}}, a separate shrine was established within the company. }}It is depicted praying to the three goddesses of Munakata Shrine, who have been praying for the protection of {{jalink|Japan|Q17}} and the {{jalink|Japanese people|Q16782073}}. Sazo wrote in his book that he believed that Ise Shrine was the ancestor of the imperial family, and Munakata Taisha Shrine was the ancestor of the people. {{jalink|Tokyo|Q1490}}{{jalink|Idemitsu Art Museum|Q3076590}} located in {{jalink|Chiyoda-ku|Q214051}} is an art museum that exhibits artworks collected by Sazo.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://idemitsu-museum.or.jp/about/outline/|title=About Idemitsu Museum of Art|accessdate=2024-09-24|website=Idemitsu Museum of Art website|publisher=Public The Idemitsu Museum of Art}} regularly holds special exhibitions such as the Munakata/Okinoshima Exhibition, and on October 17th every year, when the tea ceremony is held at Munakata Taisha Shrine, many of the famous tea utensils from the collection are put on display, and the {{jalink|Omotesenke|Q3278052}} master offers tea, commemorating the perpetuation of the shrine and remembering Sazo. === Specialty === * Munakata Taisha Shrine rice crackers * Happiness Mochi === Transportation === By bus * Hetsunomiya - From {{jalink|Kagoshima Main Line|Q1187520}}/{{jalink|Togo Station|Q5359652}}, take {{jalink|Nishitetsu Bus|Q11629843}} Route 1 bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at "Munakata Taisha-mae". It takes 10 minutes. * Nakatsumiya/Okitsumiya Yohaisho - From Togo Station on the Kagoshima Main Line, take the Nishitetsu bus bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at the last stop (20 minutes). From {{jalink|Kamiminato Fishing Port}} to {{jalink|Oshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|Q30933915|Oshima Port}}, it takes 15 minutes by the {{jalink|Munakata Municipal Ferry|Q11451853}} passenger ship, or 25 minutes by ferry. 5 minutes walk (800 meters) from Oshima Port to Nakatsunomiya. If you have your own car, it is 16 kilometers from {{jalink|Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803}}{{jalink|Wakamiya Interchange|Q1575782}} to Hetsunomiya and 19 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. Alternatively, from the same {{jalink|Koga Interchange|Q1577981}}, it is 15 kilometers to Hetsunomiya and 17 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. From Kamiminato Fishing Port, take the Munakata Municipal Ferry to Oshima Port, 400 meters to Nakatsu-miya Shrine, and 2.3 kilometers to Okitsu-miya Yohaisho. === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 59 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{jalink|Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645}}, 1979, 327 pages * Shunpei Ueyama et al., “Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines” {{jalink|Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312}}, 1992, pp. 264-265 * "Book of Shinto" {{jalink|Gakken|Q86741099|Gakken}}, 1992, p. 211 === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === References === * "Fukuoka History Walk" edited by Fukuoka City ({{jalink|Kuniomi Hirano|Q11483648}} was in charge of the maintenance of Munakata Taisha Shrine) * {{jalink|Shinya Fujiwara|Q5157839}}・{{jalink|Ryuutaro Abe|Q4721954}} "Okinoshima, the Island of the Gods" ({{jalink|Shogakukan|Q785697}} 2013) * {{Cite book |Japanese book| author = Idemitsu Museum of Art | title = Munakata Taisha National Treasure Exhibition: The Island of the Gods, Okinoshima and the sacred treasures of the shrine | publisher = Idemitsu Museum of Art, public interest incorporated foundation | year = 2014 |ref = harv}} === Related items === {{Commonscat}} * {{jalink|Munakata Shrine|Q11451876}} * {{jalink|Three goddesses of Munakata|Q10948069}} * {{jalink|Chinkokuji|Q11651157}} - The former {{jalink|Shakaku|Q10444029}} was {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System #Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}. There are over 7,000 shrines throughout Japan, including {{jalink|Munakata Shrine|Q11451876}}, {{jalink|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763}}, and {{jalink|Munakata Three Goddess It is the headquarters of the shrine that enshrines |Q10948069}}, and in ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', it is referred to as ``''Doshu Taka''''. {{jalink|Okinoshima|Q7082047}} floating in the {{jalink|Genkai Sea|Q498047}} is considered a sacred area, and many of the {{jalink|ancient|Q41493}}{{jalink|rituals}} offerings excavated on Okinoshima have been designated as {{jalink|national treasure|Q1139795}}. It is also called ``Ura Ise''.It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in {{jalink|2017|Q25290}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}29) as one of the constituent assets of '''{{jalink|"Island inhabited by the Gods" Munakata/Okinoshima and Related Heritage Group|Q324638}}'''. === Overview === Munakata Taisha is a general term for three shrines: ``Okitsu-miya'' on {{jalink|Okinoshima|Q7082047}}, ``Nakatsu-miya'' on {{jalink|Chikuzen Oshima}}, and ``Hetsu-miya'' (Soja) on Tajima, {{jalink|Munakata City|Q819603}}, but nowadays it often refers to just ``Hetsu-miya''. Hetsu Shrine is enshrined in Tajima, Munakata City, and is also called ``Tajima-sama'' by the locals. There is also Okitsu-miya Yohaisho ('''Teitsu-miya'') on Chikuzen Oshima. On the map, Nakatsu-miya, which is 11 km away from Hetsu-miya, and Okitsu-miya, which is 49 km further away, are all in a straight line. It is one of the oldest shrines in Japan, whose history is recorded in the {{jalink|Kikiki|Q842308}}, and has been a maritime route for politics, economy, and culture between the continent and the peninsula since ancient times. Since ancient times, he has been worshiped for his divine power as a {{jalink|god|Q178885}} of {{jalink|sea surface|Q125465|sea}} and {{jalink|traffic safety|Q1147899}}, but now he is worshiped not only on the sea but also on all roads, land, and traffic safety under the name of Doshu Taka.{{jalink|faith|Q5410500}}. For this reason, many {{jalink|cars|Q1420}} with Munakata Taisha Shrine {{jalink|stickers|Q2872553|stickers}} can be seen in Fukuoka Prefecture and its surrounding areas, and there are also a large number of people who purchase a new car and receive a purification at the prayer hall. Additionally, the traffic safety charms that are worn on cars originate from Munakata Taisha Shrine.Okinoshima Island, where Okitsu-miya is located, is located at a key point for maritime traffic.Since ancient times, people have been called ``Oiwasama'' because people were not allowed to enter the island and reveal what they saw or heard, and the entire island is {{jalink|go|Q11488760}}{{jalink|divine body|Q327532}}. For this reason, even today {{jalink|women are prohibited|Q11446290}}, and even men must undergo {{jalink|misogi|Q1936265}} before landing. This is sometimes said to be gender discrimination, but there is a theory that the island's god is a female god ({{jalink|Tashin Himekami}}) and that women who land on the island are said to be jealous and have a curse, but this is not confirmed. Excavations on Okinoshima Island have been carried out for more than ten years since 1952, and a large amount of ritual artifacts (offerings) such as ancient ritual remains and ornaments from the 4th to 9th centuries were discovered, as well as stone tools, pottery, and other artifacts from the {{jalink|Jomon period|Q52824}} to the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}. For this reason, Okinoshima is commonly called the ``{{jalink|Shosoin|Q2379007}}'' of the sea, and it is remembered that it has been the subject of {{jalink|faith|Q5410500}} by {{jalink|Amajin|Q9495537}} and others since prehistoric times. Currently, it is designated as an emergency evacuation port during typhoons. The plaque of {{jalink|Divine Rescript|Q11588781}} that is hung in the shrine's worship hall is {{jalink|Calligraphy|Q11498466}} by {{jalink|Prince Fushiminomiya Sadaai|Q466326}}, and the plaque at Munakata Palace is the script of Imperial Envoy Shonii Gon Dainagon, Akitaka Hamuro.{{jalink|Egypt|Q79}}{{jalink|Archaeologist|Q3621491}} {{jalink|Sakuji Yoshimura|Q2740406}} advocated A movement arose to designate the ritual sites of Noshima and the Munakata region as {{jalink|World Heritage|Q9259}}, and in 2009, "Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, Hetsu-miya" and "Okitsu-miya Yohaisho" were established. It was added to the tentative list as a group of related heritage sites including the ``Island inhabited by the Gods,'' Munakata/Okinoshima, and was nominated in 2015, and in July 2017, it was officially registered as a World Heritage Site at the {{jalink|UNESCO}} World Heritage Committee meeting in {{jalink|Poland|Q36}} and {{jalink|Krakow|Q31487}}. === Enshrined God === Each of the three shrines enshrines the following gods, collectively known as {{jalink|Three Goddesses of Munakata|Q10948069}} (Munakata Okami). * Okitsuguu Shrine: {{jalink|Takiribime|Q10932870|Tashin Himekami}} * Nakatsugu Shrine: {{jalink|Tagitsuhime|Q10932592|Tanatsu Himekami}} * Hetsu Shrine: {{jalink|Ichikishima Hime|Q11059454|Ichikishima Himekami}} File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Hetsu Shrine).JPG|Hetsu Shrine Worship Hall (photo before the construction of the shrine) File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Nakatsu Shrine Worship Hall File:Munakata Taisha Okitsu Shrine.JPG|Okitsu Shrine Worship Hall === Shrine building === [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden1.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Worship Hall]] [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden2.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Hall of Worship]] [[File:Munakata-taisha shimboku.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Sacred Tree]] [[File:Munakata-taisha museum.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Shinpokan]] === Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya === * Main shrine (first shrine, Ichikishima Hime is the enshrined deity. It was built by {{jalink|Ujisada Munakata|Q10204112}} and is said to have been based on the main shrine of Nakatsu-miya on Oshima. Important cultural property) * Hall of worship (gabled roof, with a plaque from Munakata Palace. Built by {{jalink|Takakage Kobayakawa|Q1143508}}. Important cultural property) * Second Shrine (Okitsu-miya branch shrine, enshrined as Tagori-hime) * Third shrine (Nakatsumiya branch shrine, Tagitsuhime is the enshrined deity) * Takamiya Festival Hall (The ancient ritual remains at Byetsu-miya Shrine and the Shimo-Takamiya ritual site have been protected and newly constructed directly above the site. Today, large festivals in spring and autumn, as well as rituals in the garden are still held there.) * Prayer Hall (Newly built in the Heisei period. Sakaki trees are planted in the center, and the garden is designed to look like Okinoshima Island. Various prayers are accepted at the counter.) * Ceremonial Hall (A hall dedicated to events such as weddings. The one that was previously located at Yasukuni Shrine in Tokyo was relocated.) * Seimei-den (a hall where the shrine maidens of Munakata Taisha perform dances etc.) * Imperial Embassy (a palace where the Emperor, the Imperial Family, and their imperial envoys stay when they come to the shrine for offerings.) * Shinmon (rebuilt in the Taisho period) * Handshake (a newly installed roof or cover over the approach that connects the shrine to the shrine gate.Currently, the ``Shinmon'' is in front of the shrine, and both the shrine and the main shrine can only be seen from the side.) * Haraisha (Haraito deity is enshrined in all directions) * Chozuya (There is no {{jalink|ladle|Q11533616}} and you receive water directly.) * Otorii (donated by {{jalink|Takichi Aso|Q2743525}})* Minor shrines (built in the early Edo period, a group of shrines in Munakata, Kamigun were donated by the then lord of Fukuoka, {{jalink|Mitsuyuki Kuroda|Q11678571}}, and there are about 121 shrines around the outside of the main shrine.) * Ebisusha * Matsuosha * Munakata Soreisha Shrine * Munakata Gokoku Shrine * Sacred Treasure Hall (Enjoy displaying and storing the national treasures listed below.) * Munakata Chayu (rest facility with a cafe. Donated by the Kuroda clan, the lord of Fukuoka domain.) * Torii, et al. === History ===In {{jalink|tradition|Q36192}}, it has {{jalink|origin}} in {{jalink|Japanese mythology|Q814158}}. {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602}} and {{jalink|Susanoo|Q272993|Amaterasu and Susa}} During Noo's Pledge|Q11284880|Pledge}} (Pledge), Amaterasu Omikami bit down the Sword of Suho, and the three goddesses of Munakata were born from the fragments that blew out. The origin of Munakata Taisha Shrine is said to be that the goddesses worshiped Amaterasu's ``''{{jalink|divine edict|Q11588781}}'''' and descended to the islands of Tsukushi Munakata in the Genkai Sea in the Kaihoku region to protect and help the imperial descendant {{jalink|Ninigi no Mikoto}}, and came to rule over this land. The only ``gods who descended from heaven to earth'' mentioned in {{jalink|Kiki|Q842308}} are {{jalink|Ninigi no Mikoto}} and the three goddesses of Munakata who descended from heaven before {{jalink|Descent of Tenson|Q1084733}}. This is the oldest record of the Kiki in which the names of gods and their enshrined locations are clearly described. According to the {{jalink|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664}}{{jalink|Fudōki|Q1194534}} regarding the shrine worship of Munakata Sangu Shrine, ``Saikaido Fudoki says, ``Since the time of Saimon Mountain, where Munakata Okami and his god were descended, , Ao-tama-Okikutsu-miya-no-omote, eight-shaku-purple-purple-oki-Okitsu-miya-no-omote, Yata-kagami-Okibetsu-miya-no-omote, and these three tables are placed in the form of the god's body. There is an anecdote that says, ``Sannomiya, Soku-no-in, Gin-gata-gun, Gonin-kai, descendants of Munakata Ki-Okai-no-Mikoto, and now Munakata Ason, etc.'' In ``{{jalink|Kojiki|Q813031}}'', Munakata is given the character ``Musakata,'' and is also written ``Munetakata'' or ``Munakata,'' but there is also a theory that it was originally Mizugata. It has been worshiped as the guardian deity of the local people since ancient times, and it is said that when {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803}} prayed for safe voyages during her {{jalink|Sankan Conquest|Q11249435}}, she had a miraculous experience here, and it is said that she had a habit of sending envoys to Munakata whenever the situation arises. It was valued by the {{jalink|Yamato Imperial Court}}, and since ancient times, whenever the capital was transferred, a spirit of our company was enshrined in the {{jalink|kendokoro|Q11635085}} (kashikodokoro) of the imperial court. This anecdote also reveals how he came to be worshiped as a {{jalink|guardian|Q131278957}} of safe navigation.With the introduction of {{jalink|ritsuryo system#Japanese ritsuryo system|Q742460|ritsuryo system}}, {{jalink|kokugunri system|Q11421491|kokugun system}}, {{jalink|Munakata county|Q6935606|one county of Munakata}} was given as {{jalink|Temple territory|Q11458058|Shinryo}}, The local {{jalink|gozoku|Q84066}}{{jalink|Munakata clan|Q16481907|Munegata clan}} served the shrine as {{jalink|Shinto priest|Q60523|Shinto priest}}, and also took charge of the {{jalink|administration|Q31728}} of {{jalink|Kamigun|Q11590937}}. According to the {{jalink|stone monument|Q178743}} that records the origins of the Munakata clan, the head of the Munakata clan has welcomed the daughter of a Chinese {{jalink|merchant|Q215536}} as his {{jalink|lawful wife|Q1765533}} for two generations. Also, {{jalink|Munegata Tokuzen|Q11451927}} put his daughter {{jalink|Amago Musume|Q11464914}} into the {{jalink|Inner Palace|Q5353683}} of {{jalink|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181}}, and {{jalink|Hakuji|Q540118}} for 5 years ({ The first prince, {{jalink|Prince Takaichi|Q837590}}, who was born to the two in {{jalink|654|Q31109}}, achieved great success by helping his father in the {{jalink|Jinshin War|Q2378252}}, and was later appointed as {{jalink|Dajodaijin|Q1157586}}. {{jalink|King Nagaya|Q1963492}} was the son of Takaichi and also the ancestor of the {{jalink|Takashina clan|Q11673216}}. In {{jalink|807|Q30016}} ({{jalink|Daido (Japan)|Q1373191|Daido}}2), 74 houses were donated, {{jalink|840|Q29936}} ({{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jōwa}} 7th year), he was conferred {{jalink|Junior Fifth Rank Lower}}, and then became {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōgan}} first year) and {{jalink|Senior Second Rank|Q11123277}}. In the 4th year of {{jalink|Tenkei|Q1327340}} (after the {{jalink|Tenkei War|Q11442602}}), advance further and obtain {{jalink|Shinkai|Q11591025}} of {{jalink|Shoichii|Q11123258}}. {{jalink|979|Q23784}} ({{jalink|Tengen (Japan)|Q1327101|Tengen}}2 years) The {{jalink|Grand Shrine}} position is established by {{jalink|Dajokan|Q1192939}}.After the {{jalink|Kamakura period|Q236205}}, the {{jalink|Munakata clan|Q16481907}}, who was the descendant of the Munakata clan and inherited the position of the Daiguji family, became samurai and grew into a powerful kokujin feudal lord, but during the Sengoku period, {{jalink|Ouchi clan|Q1348 909}}, {{jalink|Otomo clan|Q1096662}}, {{jalink|Shoni clan|Q2975368}}, and other nearby feudal lords were mobilized for wars, and Munakata Taisha Shrine also became the target of military attacks and was frequently arsoned and destroyed, and the Munakata clan also declined. However, each time it was worshiped by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} and {{jalink|Samurai|Q2927809}} and was repeatedly rebuilt. The current Hetsu Shrine {{jalink|main hall|Q2044994}}, with its beautiful large shingled roof, was rebuilt by the chief priest {{jalink|Ujisada Munakata|Q10204112}} in the 6th year of Tensho ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}). Ken, Hetsu-miya {{jalink|haiden|Q3125745}} was rebuilt in Tensho 16 ({{jalink|1590|Q6764}}) by {{jalink|Takakage Kobayakawa|Q1143508}}, the lord of Chikuzen. Both the main hall of worship of Hetsu Shrine are designated as national {{jalink|Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622}}. The rituals carried out by the Munakata clan were then passed on to the {{jalink|Kusakari clan}} ({{jalink|Shigetsugu Kusakari|Q22126274}}). During the Edo period, it is often reported that the {{jalink|Chikuzen|Q242409}}{{jalink|Fukuoka Domain|Q208766}} lord {{jalink|Kuroda clan|Q2975305}} constructed and repaired shrine buildings, and {{jalink|donated|Q11455717}} the shrine's territory. After that, from the end of the Edo period to the Meiji period ({{jalink|Haibutsu Kishaku|Q702298}}, Byobuyama {{jalink|Chinkokuji|Q11651157}}, which was {{jalink|Jinguji|Q1074971}}, was separated from the Taisha shrine.Also, in {{jalink|1871|Q7746}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}4), it was listed as ``Munakata Shrine'' in {{jalink|Kokuheichusha}} in the {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. On April 22 of the following year, he was promoted to {{jalink|Kanpei Chusha}}. After {{jalink|Showa|Q327567}} {{jalink|World War II|Q362}}, the shrine grounds were in ruins. Born in Akama (Akama district, Munakata city), he has worshiped Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. It was built with a donation from {{jalink|Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431}}, a businessman whom he admired, and he worked hard to encourage the government to investigate and excavate the Okinoshima ritual ruins where Okitsu Shrine is located. === Kei Yukiyuki === {{jalink|1983|Q2434}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}58), Crown Prince Akihito (later {{jalink|Emperor Empress Akihito||Retired Emperor Akihito}}) and his wife Michiko (later {{jalink|Emperor Empress Michiko|Q87610}}) visited Hetsu Shrine. {{jalink|2013|Q1998}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}25), {{jalink|Naruhito|Q217096|Crown Prince Naruhito}} visited Hetsu Shrine. {{jalink|2017|Q25290}} (2017) {{jalink|October 29|Q2951}}, Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko became the first emperors and empresses in history to visit Hetsu Shrine to pay their respects.{{Cite news|Japanese book|title=Fukuoka) Their Majesties visit Munakata Taisha, a World Heritage Site: Asahi Shimbun Digital|url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASKBY5R38KBYTIPE012.html|accessdate=2018-05-08|language=ja-JP|work=Asahi Shimbun Digital}}{{Broken link|date=March 2024}}. In addition, as a member of the imperial family, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}}'s younger brother {{jalink|archaeologist|Q3621491}} {{jalink|Prince Takahito Mikasa|Q280229}} visited the shrine many times, and he also composed waka poems about Okinoshima. === Sessha === * Kamiminato Munakata Shrine (Old Shrine) - Outside the precincts of the shrine (Autumn Grand Festival Tajima Hojokai, {{jalink|Miare Festival|Q11278738}}, where mikoshi of the three goddesses are lined up and dedicated) === Shinto rituals and festivals === * New Year's Festival - Shinto rituals to celebrate the New Year, such as Saidan Festival. 1st to 3rd of New Year every year. * Spring Festival - April 1st-3rd every year. * Summer Purification - Held at the end of July every year. * {{jalink|Tanabata|Q13423122}} Festival - Held every year on {{jalink|lunar calendar|Q11511066}} at the evening of July 7th at the Nakatsu Shrine of {{jalink|Chikuzen Oshima}}. There are {{jalink|Kengyu}}sha and {{jalink|Orijo}}sha, in front of which bamboo bamboo leaves with strips of paper are erected to pray for improvement in the craft. A ritual is held to predict the fate of men and women by looking at their reflections in the water, and a Tanabata {{jalink|calligraphy|Q11498466}} competition is also held. According to the Shohei Annual Events, it is {{jalink|1346|Q6080}} ``Tanabata Mushifuri Shinto ritual on the seventh day of July''. * Autumn Festival - October 1st to 3rd every year. Prior to the event at Hetsu Shrine's main shrine on the 1st to 3rd, there is a {{jalink|divine welcome}} ritual held at Nakatsu-miya and Okitsu-miya shrines, and a {{jalink|divine celebration||marine divine celebration}} is held with colorful flags and banners set up by fishing boats (Miare Festival). At the main shrine, {{jalink|Okina|Q11610439}} dances, customary dances, {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}}, dedication {{jalink|sumo|Q40561}}, etc. are performed. Its origins date back to the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, and its official name is ``Tajima Hojokai.'' * Kencha Festival - Held on October 17th every year. * Harvest Festival - A new festival that began to be held every year after the Heisei Emperor and Empress paid their respects to our company.* West Japan Chrysanthemum Exhibition - A chrysanthemum exhibition held every November. A large number of cultivated chrysanthemums from Kyushu and other prefectures in western Japan will be on display and appreciated. * Ancient Ceremony Festival, Hibisai Festival - A secret winter festival with a history of over 800 years that is held in mid-December every year. * New Year's Purification - New Year's Eve Shinto ritual held on New Year's Eve every year. === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * '''Items excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture/Traditional Items excavated from the Oki-tsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture'''' Bulk: A collection of artifacts excavated from over 20 ritual sites on Okinoshima, a remote island in the Genkai Sea. It was excavated during the first to third excavations from {{jalink|1954|Q18581}} to {{jalink|1971|Q2475}}. Spreads from {{jalink|Kofun period|Q459939}} to {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}} ({{jalink|4th century|Q8099}} to {{jalink|10th century|Q8052}}). The main artifacts excavated include various bronze mirrors, horse harnesses made of gilt bronze (gold plated on copper), including products from China and the Korean Peninsula, as well as Haji ware, Sansai pottery, talcum products, jade items, and swords. Among the excavated items are fragments of glass bowls thought to have been made by {{jalink|Persia}} and {{jalink|Sassanid|Q83891}}. It is an extremely valuable academic resource that contributes to research in a variety of fields, including archaeology, art history, religious history, and ancient history. The results of three excavations have been published in the form of reports called ``Okinoshima,'' ``Zoku Okinoshima,'' and ``Munakata Okinoshima.'' These excavated items are on display at the sacred treasure museum of Munakata Taisha Shrine. In {{jalink|1962|Q2764}}, the artifacts from the first and second excavations were designated as national treasures, and in {{jalink|2003|Q1986}}, the artifacts from the third excavation were additionally designated as national treasures. It is the largest national treasure in Japan in terms of quantity, consisting of approximately 80,000 relics.
