In addition, as a member of the imperial family, {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|WD=Q34479|1=Hirohito}}'s younger brother {{ill|lt=archaeologist|Q3621491|WD=Q3621491|1=Archaeologist}} {{ill|lt=Prince Takahito Mikasa|Q280229|WD=Q280229|1=Takahito, Prince Mikasa}} visited the shrine many times, and he also composed waka poems about Okinoshima. === Sessha === * Kamiminato Munakata Shrine (Old Shrine) - Outside the precincts of the shrine (Autumn Grand Festival Tajima Hojokai, {{ill|lt=Miare Festival|Q11278738|WD=Q11278738|1=Miare Festival}}, where mikoshi of the three goddesses are lined up and dedicated) === Shinto rituals and festivals === * New Year's Festival - Shinto rituals to celebrate the New Year, such as Saidan Festival. 1st to 3rd of New Year every year. * Spring Festival - April 1st-3rd every year. * Summer Purification - Held at the end of July every year. * {{ill|lt=Tanabata|Q13423122|WD=Q13423122|1=Qixi Festival}} Festival - Held every year on {{ill|lt=lunar calendar|Q11511066|WD=Q11511066|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar}} at the evening of July 7th at the Nakatsu Shrine of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chikuzen Oshima|1=UNKNOWN}}. There are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kengyu|1=UNKNOWN}}sha and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Orijo|1=UNKNOWN}}sha, in front of which bamboo bamboo leaves with strips of paper are erected to pray for improvement in the craft. A ritual is held to predict the fate of men and women by looking at their reflections in the water, and a Tanabata {{ill|lt=calligraphy|Q11498466|WD=Q11498466|1=calligraphy}} competition is also held. According to the Shohei Annual Events, it is {{ill|lt=1346|Q6080|WD=Q6080|1=1346}} ``Tanabata Mushifuri Shinto ritual on the seventh day of July''. * Autumn Festival - October 1st to 3rd every year. Prior to the event at Hetsu Shrine's main shrine on the 1st to 3rd, there is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine welcome|1=UNKNOWN}} ritual held at Nakatsu-miya and Okitsu-miya shrines, and a {{ill|lt=divine celebration|UNKNOWN|lt=marine divine celebration}} is held with colorful flags and banners set up by fishing boats (Miare Festival). At the main shrine, {{ill|lt=Okina|Q11610439|WD=Q11610439|1=okina}} dances, customary dances, {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}}, dedication {{ill|lt=sumo|Q40561|WD=Q40561|1=Sumo}}, etc. are performed. Its origins date back to the {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, and its official name is ``Tajima Hojokai.'' * Kencha Festival - Held on October 17th every year. * Harvest Festival - A new festival that began to be held every year after the Heisei Emperor and Empress paid their respects to our company.* West Japan Chrysanthemum Exhibition - A chrysanthemum exhibition held every November. A large number of cultivated chrysanthemums from Kyushu and other prefectures in western Japan will be on display and appreciated. * Ancient Ceremony Festival, Hibisai Festival - A secret winter festival with a history of over 800 years that is held in mid-December every year. * New Year's Purification - New Year's Eve Shinto ritual held on New Year's Eve every year. === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * '''Items excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture/Traditional Items excavated from the Oki-tsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture'''' Bulk: A collection of artifacts excavated from over 20 ritual sites on Okinoshima, a remote island in the Genkai Sea. It was excavated during the first to third excavations from {{ill|lt=1954|Q18581|WD=Q18581|1=1954}} to {{ill|lt=1971|Q2475|WD=Q2475|1=1971}}. Spreads from {{ill|lt=Kofun period|Q459939|WD=Q459939|1=Kofun period}} to {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}} ({{ill|lt=4th century|Q8099|WD=Q8099|1=4th century}} to {{ill|lt=10th century|Q8052|WD=Q8052|1=10th century}}). The main artifacts excavated include various bronze mirrors, horse harnesses made of gilt bronze (gold plated on copper), including products from China and the Korean Peninsula, as well as Haji ware, Sansai pottery, talcum products, jade items, and swords. Among the excavated items are fragments of glass bowls thought to have been made by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Persia|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sassanid|Q83891|WD=Q83891|1=Sasanian Empire}}. It is an extremely valuable academic resource that contributes to research in a variety of fields, including archaeology, art history, religious history, and ancient history. The results of three excavations have been published in the form of reports called ``Okinoshima,'' ``Zoku Okinoshima,'' and ``Munakata Okinoshima.'' These excavated items are on display at the sacred treasure museum of Munakata Taisha Shrine. In {{ill|lt=1962|Q2764|WD=Q2764|1=1962}}, the artifacts from the first and second excavations were designated as national treasures, and in {{ill|lt=2003|Q1986|WD=Q1986|1=2003}}, the artifacts from the third excavation were additionally designated as national treasures. It is the largest national treasure in Japan in terms of quantity, consisting of approximately 80,000 relics. === Important cultural property === * Munakata Shrine Hetsumiya Worship Hall * Munakata Shrine Hetsumiya Main Hall * A pair of wooden guardian dogs * A pair of stone guardian dogs * Aikawa Odoka Tajiro Doumaru with helmet and pot sleeves - "{{ill|lt=Doumaru|Q495328|WD=Q495328|1=Dō-maru}}" is a type of armor. * Sutra stone (Front {{ill|lt=Amida Tathagata|Q236242|WD=Q236242|1=Amitābha}} statue, back {{ill|lt=Amida Sutra|Q2661817|WD=Q2661817|1=Amitābha Sūtra}}) (Amida Buddha sutra monument) * Munakata Shrine Documents Volume 12 with attached: Munakata Shrine Records Volume 5, 1 volume, Munakata Shrine Documents Somokuroki 1 volume * 4,342 volumes of Shirojoboshi's Isshu Issukyo When it was designated as an important cultural property in 1958, there were 4,331 volumes, but 11 volumes were additionally designated in 1992 (Ministry of Education Notification No. 85, June 22, 1992). Colophon from 1187 to 1227 (Owned by Koshoji Temple, Tajima, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) * Talcstone sutra cylinder inscribed in the 4th year of the Ninpei era (owned by Inamoto Ward, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) === Historic Site (Nationally Designated) === * Munakata Shrine grounds === Fukuoka Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === * Munakata Shrine Nakatsumiya Main Hall === Others === * Compass of {{ill|lt=Battleship|Q182531|WD=Q182531|1=Battleship}}{{ill|lt=Mikasa (battleship)|Q696891|WD=Q696891|lt=Mikasa|1=Japanese battleship Mikasa}}, which was active in {{ill|lt=Battle of the Sea of Japan|Q208127|WD=Q208127|1=Battle of Tsushima}} * An Okina mask surfaced off the coast of Cape Kane in {{ill|lt=Meio|Q1193841|WD=Q1193841|1=Meiō}}8 ({{ill|lt=1499|Q6708|WD=Q6708|1=1499}}) === Munakata Taisha and Sazo Idemitsu ==={{ill|lt=Idemitsu Kosan|Q2216770|WD=Q2216770|1=Idemitsu Kosan}}'s founder, {{ill|lt=Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431|WD=Q7429431|1=Sazō Idemitsu}}, is from the former {{ill|lt=Munakata District|Q6935606|WD=Q6935606|1=Munakata District, Fukuoka}} Akama-juku, and has revered Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. In 1937, when he visited Betsu Shrine, he lamented the devastation of the shrine, and in 1942 he called for the formation of the ``Munakata Shrine Restoration Society'' and became its first president. After suspending its activities during and after the war, it was reorganized as the Munakata Taisha Reconstruction Society in 1969. The restoration of the main shrine and worship hall of Hetsu Shrine was largely due to Sazo's donations, but as he declined out of fear, there were no traces of his name within the shrine grounds for a long time, but there are now exhibits honoring Sazo at Shinpokan and other places. In the novel "{{ill|lt=A Man Called a Pirate|Q16046027|WD=Q16046027|1=A Man Called Pirate}}," which is based on Sazo, upon {{ill|lt=defeat|Q11499267|WD=Q11499267|1=defeat}}, a separate shrine was established within the company. }}It is depicted praying to the three goddesses of Munakata Shrine, who have been praying for the protection of {{ill|lt=Japan|Q17|WD=Q17|1=Japan}} and the {{ill|lt=Japanese people|Q16782073|WD=Q16782073|1=Ethnic Japanese}}. Sazo wrote in his book that he believed that Ise Shrine was the ancestor of the imperial family, and Munakata Taisha Shrine was the ancestor of the people. {{ill|lt=Tokyo|Q1490|WD=Q1490|1=Tokyo}}{{ill|lt=Idemitsu Art Museum|Q3076590|WD=Q3076590|1=Idemitsu Museum of Arts}} located in {{ill|lt=Chiyoda-ku|Q214051|WD=Q214051|1=Chiyoda, Tokyo}} is an art museum that exhibits artworks collected by Sazo.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://idemitsu-museum.or.jp/about/outline/|title=About Idemitsu Museum of Art|accessdate=2024-09-24|website=Idemitsu Museum of Art website|publisher=Public The Idemitsu Museum of Art}} regularly holds special exhibitions such as the Munakata/Okinoshima Exhibition, and on October 17th every year, when the tea ceremony is held at Munakata Taisha Shrine, many of the famous tea utensils from the collection are put on display, and the {{ill|lt=Omotesenke|Q3278052|WD=Q3278052|1=Omotesenke}} master offers tea, commemorating the perpetuation of the shrine and remembering Sazo. === Specialty === * Munakata Taisha Shrine rice crackers * Happiness Mochi === Transportation === By bus * Hetsunomiya - From {{ill|lt=Kagoshima Main Line|Q1187520|WD=Q1187520|1=Kagoshima Main Line}}/{{ill|lt=Togo Station|Q5359652|WD=Q5359652|1=Tōgō Station}}, take {{ill|lt=Nishitetsu Bus|Q11629843|WD=Q11629843|1=Nishitetsu Bus}} Route 1 bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at "Munakata Taisha-mae". It takes 10 minutes. * Nakatsumiya/Okitsumiya Yohaisho - From Togo Station on the Kagoshima Main Line, take the Nishitetsu bus bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at the last stop (20 minutes). From {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiminato Fishing Port|1=UNKNOWN}} to {{ill|lt=Oshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|Q30933915|WD=Q30933915|lt=Oshima Port|1=Port of Oshima}}, it takes 15 minutes by the {{ill|lt=Munakata Municipal Ferry|Q11451853|WD=Q11451853|1=Munakata Municipal Ferry}} passenger ship, or 25 minutes by ferry. 5 minutes walk (800 meters) from Oshima Port to Nakatsunomiya. If you have your own car, it is 16 kilometers from {{ill|lt=Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803|WD=Q1060803|1=Kyushu Expressway}}{{ill|lt=Wakamiya Interchange|Q1575782|WD=Q1575782|1=Wakamiya interchange}} to Hetsunomiya and 19 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. Alternatively, from the same {{ill|lt=Koga Interchange|Q1577981|WD=Q1577981|1=Koga interchange}}, it is 15 kilometers to Hetsunomiya and 17 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. The former {{ill|lt=Shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System #Government Shrine|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, and currently it is {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. There are over 7,000 shrines throughout Japan, including {{ill|lt=Munakata Shrine|Q11451876|WD=Q11451876|1=Munakata Shrines}}, {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|WD=Q191763|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, and {{ill|lt=Munakata Three Goddess It is the headquarters of the shrine that enshrines|Q10948069|WD=Q10948069|1=Three Munakata Goddesses}}, and in ``{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', it is referred to as ``''Doshu Taka''''. {{ill|lt=Okinoshima|Q7082047|WD=Q7082047|1=Okinoshima (Fukuoka)}} floating in the {{ill|lt=Genkai Sea|Q498047|WD=Q498047|1=Genkai Sea}} is considered a sacred area, and many of the {{ill|lt=ancient|Q41493|WD=Q41493|1=Ancient history}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rituals|1=UNKNOWN}} offerings excavated on Okinoshima have been designated as {{ill|lt=national treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}. It is also called ``Ura Ise''.It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in {{ill|lt=2017|Q25290|WD=Q25290|1=2017}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}29) as one of the constituent assets of '''{{ill|lt="Island inhabited by the Gods" Munakata/Okinoshima and Related Heritage Group|Q324638|WD=Q324638|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region}}'''. === Overview === Munakata Taisha is a general term for three shrines: ``Okitsu-miya'' on {{ill|lt=Okinoshima|Q7082047|WD=Q7082047|1=Okinoshima (Fukuoka)}}, ``Nakatsu-miya'' on {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chikuzen Oshima|1=UNKNOWN}}, and ``Hetsu-miya'' (Soja) on Tajima, {{ill|lt=Munakata City|Q819603|WD=Q819603|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, but nowadays it often refers to just ``Hetsu-miya''. Hetsu Shrine is enshrined in Tajima, Munakata City, and is also called ``Tajima-sama'' by the locals. There is also Okitsu-miya Yohaisho ('''Teitsu-miya'') on Chikuzen Oshima. On the map, Nakatsu-miya, which is 11 km away from Hetsu-miya, and Okitsu-miya, which is 49 km further away, are all in a straight line. It is one of the oldest shrines in Japan, whose history is recorded in the {{ill|lt=Kikiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}, and has been a maritime route for politics, economy, and culture between the continent and the peninsula since ancient times. Since ancient times, he has been worshiped for his divine power as a {{ill|lt=god|Q178885|WD=Q178885|1=Deity}} of {{ill|lt=sea surface|Q125465|WD=Q125465|lt=sea|1=Sea level}} and {{ill|lt=traffic safety|Q1147899|WD=Q1147899|1=Road safety}}, but now he is worshiped not only on the sea but also on all roads, land, and traffic safety under the name of Doshu Taka.{{ill|lt=faith|Q5410500|WD=Q5410500|1=Faith}}. For this reason, many {{ill|lt=cars|Q1420|WD=Q1420|1=Car}} with Munakata Taisha Shrine {{ill|lt=stickers|Q2872553|WD=Q2872553|lt=stickers|1=Sticker}} can be seen in Fukuoka Prefecture and its surrounding areas, and there are also a large number of people who purchase a new car and receive a purification at the prayer hall. Additionally, the traffic safety charms that are worn on cars originate from Munakata Taisha Shrine.Okinoshima Island, where Okitsu-miya is located, is located at a key point for maritime traffic.Since ancient times, people have been called ``Oiwasama'' because people were not allowed to enter the island and reveal what they saw or heard, and the entire island is {{ill|lt=go|Q11488760|WD=Q11488760|1=御}}{{ill|lt=divine body|Q327532|WD=Q327532|1=Shintai}}. For this reason, even today {{ill|lt=women are prohibited|Q11446290|WD=Q11446290|1=Nyonin Kinsei}}, and even men must undergo {{ill|lt=misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265|1=Misogi}} before landing. This is sometimes said to be gender discrimination, but there is a theory that the island's god is a female god ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tashin Himekami|1=UNKNOWN}}) and that women who land on the island are said to be jealous and have a curse, but this is not confirmed. Excavations on Okinoshima Island have been carried out for more than ten years since 1952, and a large amount of ritual artifacts (offerings) such as ancient ritual remains and ornaments from the 4th to 9th centuries were discovered, as well as stone tools, pottery, and other artifacts from the {{ill|lt=Jomon period|Q52824|WD=Q52824|1=Jōmon period}} to the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. For this reason, Okinoshima is commonly called the ``{{ill|lt=Shosoin|Q2379007|WD=Q2379007|1=Shōsōin}}'' of the sea, and it is remembered that it has been the subject of {{ill|lt=faith|Q5410500|WD=Q5410500|1=Faith}} by {{ill|lt=Amajin|Q9495537|WD=Q9495537|1=Ama People}} and others since prehistoric times. Currently, it is designated as an emergency evacuation port during typhoons. The plaque of {{ill|lt=Divine Rescript|Q11588781|WD=Q11588781|1=Commandment}} that is hung in the shrine's worship hall is {{ill|lt=Calligraphy|Q11498466|WD=Q11498466|1=Calligraphy}} by {{ill|lt=Prince Fushiminomiya Sadaai|Q466326|WD=Q466326|1=Prince Fushimi Sadanaru}}, and the plaque at Munakata Palace is the script of Imperial Envoy Shonii Gon Dainagon, Akitaka Hamuro.{{ill|lt=Egypt|Q79|WD=Q79|1=Egypt}}{{ill|lt=Archaeologist|Q3621491|WD=Q3621491|1=Archaeologist}} {{ill|lt=Sakuji Yoshimura|Q2740406|WD=Q2740406|1=Sakuji Yoshimura}} advocated A movement arose to designate the ritual sites of Noshima and the Munakata region as {{ill|lt=World Heritage|Q9259|WD=Q9259|1=World Heritage Site}}, and in 2009, "Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, Hetsu-miya" and "Okitsu-miya Yohaisho" were established. It was added to the tentative list as a group of related heritage sites including the ``Island inhabited by the Gods,'' Munakata/Okinoshima, and was nominated in 2015, and in July 2017, it was officially registered as a World Heritage Site at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=UNESCO|1=UNKNOWN}} World Heritage Committee meeting in {{ill|lt=Poland|Q36|WD=Q36|1=Poland}} and {{ill|lt=Krakow|Q31487|WD=Q31487|1=Kraków}}. === Enshrined God === Each of the three shrines enshrines the following gods, collectively known as {{ill|lt=Three Goddesses of Munakata|Q10948069|WD=Q10948069|1=Three Munakata Goddesses}} (Munakata Okami). * Okitsuguu Shrine: {{ill|lt=Takiribime|Q10932870|WD=Q10932870|lt=Tashin Himekami|1=Tagorihime}} * Nakatsugu Shrine: {{ill|lt=Tagitsuhime|Q10932592|WD=Q10932592|lt=Tanatsu Himekami|1=Tagitsuhime}} * Hetsu Shrine: {{ill|lt=Ichikishima Hime|Q11059454|WD=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishima Himekami|1=Ichikishima-hime}} File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Hetsu Shrine).JPG|Hetsu Shrine Worship Hall (photo before the construction of the shrine) File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Nakatsu Shrine Worship Hall File:Munakata Taisha Okitsu Shrine.JPG|Okitsu Shrine Worship Hall === Shrine building === [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden1.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Worship Hall]] [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden2.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Hall of Worship]] [[File:Munakata-taisha shimboku.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Sacred Tree]] [[File:Munakata-taisha museum.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Shinpokan]] === Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya === * Main shrine (first shrine, Ichikishima Hime is the enshrined deity. It was built by {{ill|lt=Ujisada Munakata|Q10204112|WD=Q10204112|1=Munakata Ujisada}} and is said to have been based on the main shrine of Nakatsu-miya on Oshima. Important cultural property) * Hall of worship (gabled roof, with a plaque from Munakata Palace. Built by {{ill|lt=Takakage Kobayakawa|Q1143508|WD=Q1143508|1=Kobayakawa Takakage}}. Donated by the Kuroda clan, the lord of Fukuoka domain.) * Torii, et al. === History ===In {{ill|lt=tradition|Q36192|WD=Q36192|1=Folklore}}, it has {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=origin|1=UNKNOWN}} in {{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|1=Japanese mythology}}. {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}} and {{ill|lt=Susanoo|Q272993|WD=Q272993|lt=Amaterasu and Susa|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} During Noo's Pledge|Q11284880|Pledge}} (Pledge), Amaterasu Omikami bit down the Sword of Suho, and the three goddesses of Munakata were born from the fragments that blew out. The origin of Munakata Taisha Shrine is said to be that the goddesses worshiped Amaterasu's ``''{{ill|lt=divine edict|Q11588781|WD=Q11588781|1=Commandment}}'''' and descended to the islands of Tsukushi Munakata in the Genkai Sea in the Kaihoku region to protect and help the imperial descendant {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, and came to rule over this land. The only ``gods who descended from heaven to earth'' mentioned in {{ill|lt=Kiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}} are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} and the three goddesses of Munakata who descended from heaven before {{ill|lt=Descent of Tenson|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}}. This is the oldest record of the Kiki in which the names of gods and their enshrined locations are clearly described. According to the {{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664|1=Chikuzen Province}}{{ill|lt=Fudōki|Q1194534|WD=Q1194534|1=Fudoki}} regarding the shrine worship of Munakata Sangu Shrine, ``Saikaido Fudoki says, ``Since the time of Saimon Mountain, where Munakata Okami and his god were descended, , Ao-tama-Okikutsu-miya-no-omote, eight-shaku-purple-purple-oki-Okitsu-miya-no-omote, Yata-kagami-Okibetsu-miya-no-omote, and these three tables are placed in the form of the god's body. There is an anecdote that says, ``Sannomiya, Soku-no-in, Gin-gata-gun, Gonin-kai, descendants of Munakata Ki-Okai-no-Mikoto, and now Munakata Ason, etc.'' In ``{{ill|lt=Kojiki|Q813031|WD=Q813031|1=Kojiki}}'', Munakata is given the character ``Musakata,'' and is also written ``Munetakata'' or ``Munakata,'' but there is also a theory that it was originally Mizugata. It has been worshiped as the guardian deity of the local people since ancient times, and it is said that when {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} prayed for safe voyages during her {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}}, she had a miraculous experience here, and it is said that she had a habit of sending envoys to Munakata whenever the situation arises. It was valued by the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamato Imperial Court|1=UNKNOWN}}, and since ancient times, whenever the capital was transferred, a spirit of our company was enshrined in the {{ill|lt=kendokoro|Q11635085|WD=Q11635085|1=Kashiko-dokoro}} (kashikodokoro) of the imperial court. This anecdote also reveals how he came to be worshiped as a {{ill|lt=guardian|Q131278957|WD=Q131278957|1=Guardian deities}} of safe navigation.With the introduction of {{ill|lt=ritsuryo system#Japanese ritsuryo system|Q742460|WD=Q742460|lt=ritsuryo system|1=Ritsuryō}}, {{ill|lt=kokugunri system|Q11421491|WD=Q11421491|lt=kokugun system|1=province-district-township system}}, {{ill|lt=Munakata county|Q6935606|WD=Q6935606|lt=one county of Munakata|1=Munakata District, Fukuoka}} was given as {{ill|lt=Temple territory|Q11458058|WD=Q11458058|lt=Shinryo|1=Jisha-ryō}}, The local {{ill|lt=gozoku|Q84066|WD=Q84066|1=Gōzoku}}{{ill|lt=Munakata clan|Q16481907|WD=Q16481907|lt=Munegata clan|1=Munakata clan}} served the shrine as {{ill|lt=Shinto priest|Q60523|WD=Q60523|lt=Shinto priest|1=Kannushi}}, and also took charge of the {{ill|lt=administration|Q31728|WD=Q31728|1=Public administration}} of {{ill|lt=Kamigun|Q11590937|WD=Q11590937|1=Kamigun}}. According to the {{ill|lt=stone monument|Q178743|WD=Q178743|1=Stele}} that records the origins of the Munakata clan, the head of the Munakata clan has welcomed the daughter of a Chinese {{ill|lt=merchant|Q215536|WD=Q215536|1=Merchant}} as his {{ill|lt=lawful wife|Q1765533|WD=Q1765533|1=Seishitsu}} for two generations. Also, {{ill|lt=Munegata Tokuzen|Q11451927|WD=Q11451927|1=Munakata no Tokuzen}} put his daughter {{ill|lt=Amago Musume|Q11464914|WD=Q11464914|1=Amako no iratsume}} into the {{ill|lt=Inner Palace|Q5353683|WD=Q5353683|1=back palace}} of {{ill|lt=Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|WD=Q335181|1=Emperor Tenmu}}, and {{ill|lt=Hakuji|Q540118|WD=Q540118|1=Hakuchi (era)}} for 5 years ({ The first prince, {{ill|lt=Prince Takaichi|Q837590|WD=Q837590|1=Prince Takechi}}, who was born to the two in {{ill|lt=654|Q31109|WD=Q31109|1=654}}, achieved great success by helping his father in the {{ill|lt=Jinshin War|Q2378252|WD=Q2378252|1=Jinshin War}}, and was later appointed as {{ill|lt=Dajodaijin|Q1157586|WD=Q1157586|1=Daijō-daijin}}. {{ill|lt=King Nagaya|Q1963492|WD=Q1963492|1=Prince Nagaya}} was the son of Takaichi and also the ancestor of the {{ill|lt=Takashina clan|Q11673216|WD=Q11673216|1=Takashina clan}}. In {{ill|lt=807|Q30016|WD=Q30016|1=807}} ({{ill|lt=Daido (Japan)|Q1373191|WD=Q1373191|lt=Daido|1=Daidō}}2), 74 houses were donated, {{ill|lt=840|Q29936|WD=Q29936|1=840}} ({{ill|lt=Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|WD=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa|1=Jōwa (Heian period)}} 7th year), he was conferred {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}}, and then became {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}} first year) and {{ill|lt=Senior Second Rank|Q11123277|WD=Q11123277|1=Senior Second Rank}}. In the 4th year of {{ill|lt=Tenkei|Q1327340|WD=Q1327340|1=Tengyō}} (after the {{ill|lt=Tenkei War|Q11442602|WD=Q11442602|1=Tenkei War}}), advance further and obtain {{ill|lt=Shinkai|Q11591025|WD=Q11591025|1=Shinkai (divine rank)}} of {{ill|lt=Shoichii|Q11123258|WD=Q11123258|1=Senior First Rank}}. {{ill|lt=979|Q23784|WD=Q23784|1=979}} ({{ill|lt=Tengen (Japan)|Q1327101|WD=Q1327101|lt=Tengen|1=Tengen (era)}}2 years) The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Grand Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} position is established by {{ill|lt=Dajokan|Q1192939|WD=Q1192939|1=Daijō-kan}}.After the {{ill|lt=Kamakura period|Q236205|WD=Q236205|1=Kamakura period}}, the {{ill|lt=Munakata clan|Q16481907|WD=Q16481907|1=Munakata clan}}, who was the descendant of the Munakata clan and inherited the position of the Daiguji family, became samurai and grew into a powerful kokujin feudal lord, but during the Sengoku period, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ouchi clan|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Otomo clan|Q1096662|WD=Q1096662|1=Ōtomo clan}}, {{ill|lt=Shoni clan|Q2975368|WD=Q2975368|1=Shōni clan}}, and other nearby feudal lords were mobilized for wars, and Munakata Taisha Shrine also became the target of military attacks and was frequently arsoned and destroyed, and the Munakata clan also declined. However, each time it was worshiped by the {{ill|lt=Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|WD=Q30253177|lt=Imperial Court|1=Imperial Court of Japan}} and {{ill|lt=Samurai|Q2927809|WD=Q2927809|1=Buke}} and was repeatedly rebuilt. The current Hetsu Shrine {{ill|lt=main hall|Q2044994|WD=Q2044994|1=Honden}}, with its beautiful large shingled roof, was rebuilt by the chief priest {{ill|lt=Ujisada Munakata|Q10204112|WD=Q10204112|1=Munakata Ujisada}} in the 6th year of Tensho ({{ill|lt=1578|Q6707|WD=Q6707|1=1578}}). Ken, Hetsu-miya {{ill|lt=haiden|Q3125745|WD=Q3125745|1=Haiden (Shinto)}} was rebuilt in Tensho 16 ({{ill|lt=1590|Q6764|WD=Q6764|1=1590}}) by {{ill|lt=Takakage Kobayakawa|Q1143508|WD=Q1143508|1=Kobayakawa Takakage}}, the lord of Chikuzen. Both the main hall of worship of Hetsu Shrine are designated as national {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}. The rituals carried out by the Munakata clan were then passed on to the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kusakari clan|1=UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=Shigetsugu Kusakari|Q22126274|WD=Q22126274|1=Shigetsugu Kusakari}}). During the Edo period, it is often reported that the {{ill|lt=Chikuzen|Q242409|WD=Q242409|1=Chikuzen}}{{ill|lt=Fukuoka Domain|Q208766|WD=Q208766|1=Fukuoka Domain}} lord {{ill|lt=Kuroda clan|Q2975305|WD=Q2975305|1=Kuroda clan}} constructed and repaired shrine buildings, and {{ill|lt=donated|Q11455717|WD=Q11455717|1=contribution}} the shrine's territory. After that, from the end of the Edo period to the Meiji period ({{ill|lt=Haibutsu Kishaku|Q702298|WD=Q702298|1=Haibutsu kishaku}}, Byobuyama {{ill|lt=Chinkokuji|Q11651157|WD=Q11651157|1=Chinkoku-ji}}, which was {{ill|lt=Jinguji|Q1074971|WD=Q1074971|1=Jingū-ji}}, was separated from the Taisha shrine.Also, in {{ill|lt=1871|Q7746|WD=Q7746|1=1871}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}4), it was listed as ``Munakata Shrine'' in {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}} in the {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}. On April 22 of the following year, he was promoted to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kanpei Chusha|1=UNKNOWN}}. Then, on July 11, {{ill|lt=1901|Q2035|WD=Q2035|1=1901}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}34), it was promoted to the highest rank, {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}. After {{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}} {{ill|lt=World War II|Q362|WD=Q362|1=World War II}}, the shrine grounds were in ruins. Born in Akama (Akama district, Munakata city), he has worshiped Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. It was built with a donation from {{ill|lt=Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431|WD=Q7429431|1=Sazō Idemitsu}}, a businessman whom he admired, and he worked hard to encourage the government to investigate and excavate the Okinoshima ritual ruins where Okitsu Shrine is located. === Kei Yukiyuki === {{ill|lt=1983|Q2434|WD=Q2434|1=1983}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}58), Crown Prince Akihito (later {{ill|lt=Emperor Empress Akihito|UNKNOWN|lt=Retired Emperor Akihito}}) and his wife Michiko (later {{ill|lt=Emperor Empress Michiko|Q87610|WD=Q87610|1=Empress Michiko}}) visited Hetsu Shrine. {{ill|lt=2013|Q1998|WD=Q1998|1=2013}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}25), {{ill|lt=Naruhito|Q217096|WD=Q217096|lt=Crown Prince Naruhito|1=Naruhito}} visited Hetsu Shrine. {{ill|lt=2017|Q25290|WD=Q25290|1=2017}} (2017) {{ill|lt=October 29|Q2951|WD=Q2951|1=October 29}}, Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko became the first emperors and empresses in history to visit Hetsu Shrine to pay their respects.{{Cite news|Japanese book|title=Fukuoka) Their Majesties visit Munakata Taisha, a World Heritage Site: Asahi Shimbun Digital|url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASKBY5R38KBYTIPE012.html|accessdate=2018-05-08|language=ja-JP|work=Asahi Shimbun Digital}}{{Broken link|date=March 2024}}. In addition, as a member of the imperial family, {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|WD=Q34479|1=Hirohito}}'s younger brother {{ill|lt=archaeologist|Q3621491|WD=Q3621491|1=Archaeologist}} {{ill|lt=Prince Takahito Mikasa|Q280229|WD=Q280229|1=Takahito, Prince Mikasa}} visited the shrine many times, and he also composed waka poems about Okinoshima. === Sessha === * Kamiminato Munakata Shrine (Old Shrine) - Outside the precincts of the shrine (Autumn Grand Festival Tajima Hojokai, {{ill|lt=Miare Festival|Q11278738|WD=Q11278738|1=Miare Festival}}, where mikoshi of the three goddesses are lined up and dedicated) === Shinto rituals and festivals === * New Year's Festival - Shinto rituals to celebrate the New Year, such as Saidan Festival. 1st to 3rd of New Year every year. * Spring Festival - April 1st-3rd every year. * Summer Purification - Held at the end of July every year. * {{ill|lt=Tanabata|Q13423122|WD=Q13423122|1=Qixi Festival}} Festival - Held every year on {{ill|lt=lunar calendar|Q11511066|WD=Q11511066|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar}} at the evening of July 7th at the Nakatsu Shrine of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chikuzen Oshima|1=UNKNOWN}}. There are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kengyu|1=UNKNOWN}}sha and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Orijo|1=UNKNOWN}}sha, in front of which bamboo bamboo leaves with strips of paper are erected to pray for improvement in the craft. A ritual is held to predict the fate of men and women by looking at their reflections in the water, and a Tanabata {{ill|lt=calligraphy|Q11498466|WD=Q11498466|1=calligraphy}} competition is also held. According to the Shohei Annual Events, it is {{ill|lt=1346|Q6080|WD=Q6080|1=1346}} ``Tanabata Mushifuri Shinto ritual on the seventh day of July''. * Autumn Festival - October 1st to 3rd every year. Prior to the event at Hetsu Shrine's main shrine on the 1st to 3rd, there is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine welcome|1=UNKNOWN}} ritual held at Nakatsu-miya and Okitsu-miya shrines, and a {{ill|lt=divine celebration|UNKNOWN|lt=marine divine celebration}} is held with colorful flags and banners set up by fishing boats (Miare Festival). At the main shrine, {{ill|lt=Okina|Q11610439|WD=Q11610439|1=okina}} dances, customary dances, {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}}, dedication {{ill|lt=sumo|Q40561|WD=Q40561|1=Sumo}}, etc. are performed. Its origins date back to the {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, and its official name is ``Tajima Hojokai.'' * Kencha Festival - Held on October 17th every year. * Harvest Festival - A new festival that began to be held every year after the Heisei Emperor and Empress paid their respects to our company.* West Japan Chrysanthemum Exhibition - A chrysanthemum exhibition held every November. A large number of cultivated chrysanthemums from Kyushu and other prefectures in western Japan will be on display and appreciated. * Ancient Ceremony Festival, Hibisai Festival - A secret winter festival with a history of over 800 years that is held in mid-December every year. * New Year's Purification - New Year's Eve Shinto ritual held on New Year's Eve every year. === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * '''Items excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture/Traditional Items excavated from the Oki-tsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture'''' Bulk: A collection of artifacts excavated from over 20 ritual sites on Okinoshima, a remote island in the Genkai Sea. It was excavated during the first to third excavations from {{ill|lt=1954|Q18581|WD=Q18581|1=1954}} to {{ill|lt=1971|Q2475|WD=Q2475|1=1971}}. Spreads from {{ill|lt=Kofun period|Q459939|WD=Q459939|1=Kofun period}} to {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}} ({{ill|lt=4th century|Q8099|WD=Q8099|1=4th century}} to {{ill|lt=10th century|Q8052|WD=Q8052|1=10th century}}). The main artifacts excavated include various bronze mirrors, horse harnesses made of gilt bronze (gold plated on copper), including products from China and the Korean Peninsula, as well as Haji ware, Sansai pottery, talcum products, jade items, and swords. Among the excavated items are fragments of glass bowls thought to have been made by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Persia|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sassanid|Q83891|WD=Q83891|1=Sasanian Empire}}. It is an extremely valuable academic resource that contributes to research in a variety of fields, including archaeology, art history, religious history, and ancient history. The results of three excavations have been published in the form of reports called ``Okinoshima,'' ``Zoku Okinoshima,'' and ``Munakata Okinoshima.'' These excavated items are on display at the sacred treasure museum of Munakata Taisha Shrine. In {{ill|lt=1962|Q2764|WD=Q2764|1=1962}}, the artifacts from the first and second excavations were designated as national treasures, and in {{ill|lt=2003|Q1986|WD=Q1986|1=2003}}, the artifacts from the third excavation were additionally designated as national treasures. It is the largest national treasure in Japan in terms of quantity, consisting of approximately 80,000 relics. Colophon from 1187 to 1227 (Owned by Koshoji Temple, Tajima, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) * Talcstone sutra cylinder inscribed in the 4th year of the Ninpei era (owned by Inamoto Ward, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) === Historic Site (Nationally Designated) === * Munakata Shrine grounds === Fukuoka Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === * Munakata Shrine Nakatsumiya Main Hall === Others === * Compass of {{ill|lt=Battleship|Q182531|WD=Q182531|1=Battleship}}{{ill|lt=Mikasa (battleship)|Q696891|WD=Q696891|lt=Mikasa|1=Japanese battleship Mikasa}}, which was active in {{ill|lt=Battle of the Sea of Japan|Q208127|WD=Q208127|1=Battle of Tsushima}} * An Okina mask surfaced off the coast of Cape Kane in {{ill|lt=Meio|Q1193841|WD=Q1193841|1=Meiō}}8 ({{ill|lt=1499|Q6708|WD=Q6708|1=1499}}) === Munakata Taisha and Sazo Idemitsu ==={{ill|lt=Idemitsu Kosan|Q2216770|WD=Q2216770|1=Idemitsu Kosan}}'s founder, {{ill|lt=Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431|WD=Q7429431|1=Sazō Idemitsu}}, is from the former {{ill|lt=Munakata District|Q6935606|WD=Q6935606|1=Munakata District, Fukuoka}} Akama-juku, and has revered Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. In 1937, when he visited Betsu Shrine, he lamented the devastation of the shrine, and in 1942 he called for the formation of the ``Munakata Shrine Restoration Society'' and became its first president. After suspending its activities during and after the war, it was reorganized as the Munakata Taisha Reconstruction Society in 1969. The restoration of the main shrine and worship hall of Hetsu Shrine was largely due to Sazo's donations, but as he declined out of fear, there were no traces of his name within the shrine grounds for a long time, but there are now exhibits honoring Sazo at Shinpokan and other places. In the novel "{{ill|lt=A Man Called a Pirate|Q16046027|WD=Q16046027|1=A Man Called Pirate}}," which is based on Sazo, upon {{ill|lt=defeat|Q11499267|WD=Q11499267|1=defeat}}, a separate shrine was established within the company. }}It is depicted praying to the three goddesses of Munakata Shrine, who have been praying for the protection of {{ill|lt=Japan|Q17|WD=Q17|1=Japan}} and the {{ill|lt=Japanese people|Q16782073|WD=Q16782073|1=Ethnic Japanese}}. Sazo wrote in his book that he believed that Ise Shrine was the ancestor of the imperial family, and Munakata Taisha Shrine was the ancestor of the people. {{ill|lt=Tokyo|Q1490|WD=Q1490|1=Tokyo}}{{ill|lt=Idemitsu Art Museum|Q3076590|WD=Q3076590|1=Idemitsu Museum of Arts}} located in {{ill|lt=Chiyoda-ku|Q214051|WD=Q214051|1=Chiyoda, Tokyo}} is an art museum that exhibits artworks collected by Sazo.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://idemitsu-museum.or.jp/about/outline/|title=About Idemitsu Museum of Art|accessdate=2024-09-24|website=Idemitsu Museum of Art website|publisher=Public The Idemitsu Museum of Art}} regularly holds special exhibitions such as the Munakata/Okinoshima Exhibition, and on October 17th every year, when the tea ceremony is held at Munakata Taisha Shrine, many of the famous tea utensils from the collection are put on display, and the {{ill|lt=Omotesenke|Q3278052|WD=Q3278052|1=Omotesenke}} master offers tea, commemorating the perpetuation of the shrine and remembering Sazo. === Specialty === * Munakata Taisha Shrine rice crackers * Happiness Mochi === Transportation === By bus * Hetsunomiya - From {{ill|lt=Kagoshima Main Line|Q1187520|WD=Q1187520|1=Kagoshima Main Line}}/{{ill|lt=Togo Station|Q5359652|WD=Q5359652|1=Tōgō Station}}, take {{ill|lt=Nishitetsu Bus|Q11629843|WD=Q11629843|1=Nishitetsu Bus}} Route 1 bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at "Munakata Taisha-mae". It takes 10 minutes. * Nakatsumiya/Okitsumiya Yohaisho - From Togo Station on the Kagoshima Main Line, take the Nishitetsu bus bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at the last stop (20 minutes). From {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiminato Fishing Port|1=UNKNOWN}} to {{ill|lt=Oshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|Q30933915|WD=Q30933915|lt=Oshima Port|1=Port of Oshima}}, it takes 15 minutes by the {{ill|lt=Munakata Municipal Ferry|Q11451853|WD=Q11451853|1=Munakata Municipal Ferry}} passenger ship, or 25 minutes by ferry. 5 minutes walk (800 meters) from Oshima Port to Nakatsunomiya. If you have your own car, it is 16 kilometers from {{ill|lt=Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803|WD=Q1060803|1=Kyushu Expressway}}{{ill|lt=Wakamiya Interchange|Q1575782|WD=Q1575782|1=Wakamiya interchange}} to Hetsunomiya and 19 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. Alternatively, from the same {{ill|lt=Koga Interchange|Q1577981|WD=Q1577981|1=Koga interchange}}, it is 15 kilometers to Hetsunomiya and 17 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. The former {{ill|lt=Shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System #Government Shrine|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, and currently it is {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. There are over 7,000 shrines throughout Japan, including {{ill|lt=Munakata Shrine|Q11451876|WD=Q11451876|1=Munakata Shrines}}, {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|WD=Q191763|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, and {{ill|lt=Munakata Three Goddess It is the headquarters of the shrine that enshrines|Q10948069|WD=Q10948069|1=Three Munakata Goddesses}}, and in ``{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', it is referred to as ``''Doshu Taka''''. {{ill|lt=Okinoshima|Q7082047|WD=Q7082047|1=Okinoshima (Fukuoka)}} floating in the {{ill|lt=Genkai Sea|Q498047|WD=Q498047|1=Genkai Sea}} is considered a sacred area, and many of the {{ill|lt=ancient|Q41493|WD=Q41493|1=Ancient history}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rituals|1=UNKNOWN}} offerings excavated on Okinoshima have been designated as {{ill|lt=national treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}. It is also called ``Ura Ise''.It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in {{ill|lt=2017|Q25290|WD=Q25290|1=2017}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}29) as one of the constituent assets of '''{{ill|lt="Island inhabited by the Gods" Munakata/Okinoshima and Related Heritage Group|Q324638|WD=Q324638|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region}}'''. === Overview === Munakata Taisha is a general term for three shrines: ``Okitsu-miya'' on {{ill|lt=Okinoshima|Q7082047|WD=Q7082047|1=Okinoshima (Fukuoka)}}, ``Nakatsu-miya'' on {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chikuzen Oshima|1=UNKNOWN}}, and ``Hetsu-miya'' (Soja) on Tajima, {{ill|lt=Munakata City|Q819603|WD=Q819603|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, but nowadays it often refers to just ``Hetsu-miya''. Hetsu Shrine is enshrined in Tajima, Munakata City, and is also called ``Tajima-sama'' by the locals. There is also Okitsu-miya Yohaisho ('''Teitsu-miya'') on Chikuzen Oshima. On the map, Nakatsu-miya, which is 11 km away from Hetsu-miya, and Okitsu-miya, which is 49 km further away, are all in a straight line. It is one of the oldest shrines in Japan, whose history is recorded in the {{ill|lt=Kikiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}, and has been a maritime route for politics, economy, and culture between the continent and the peninsula since ancient times. Since ancient times, he has been worshiped for his divine power as a {{ill|lt=god|Q178885|WD=Q178885|1=Deity}} of {{ill|lt=sea surface|Q125465|WD=Q125465|lt=sea|1=Sea level}} and {{ill|lt=traffic safety|Q1147899|WD=Q1147899|1=Road safety}}, but now he is worshiped not only on the sea but also on all roads, land, and traffic safety under the name of Doshu Taka.{{ill|lt=faith|Q5410500|WD=Q5410500|1=Faith}}. For this reason, many {{ill|lt=cars|Q1420|WD=Q1420|1=Car}} with Munakata Taisha Shrine {{ill|lt=stickers|Q2872553|WD=Q2872553|lt=stickers|1=Sticker}} can be seen in Fukuoka Prefecture and its surrounding areas, and there are also a large number of people who purchase a new car and receive a purification at the prayer hall. Additionally, the traffic safety charms that are worn on cars originate from Munakata Taisha Shrine.Okinoshima Island, where Okitsu-miya is located, is located at a key point for maritime traffic.Since ancient times, people have been called ``Oiwasama'' because people were not allowed to enter the island and reveal what they saw or heard, and the entire island is {{ill|lt=go|Q11488760|WD=Q11488760|1=御}}{{ill|lt=divine body|Q327532|WD=Q327532|1=Shintai}}. For this reason, even today {{ill|lt=women are prohibited|Q11446290|WD=Q11446290|1=Nyonin Kinsei}}, and even men must undergo {{ill|lt=misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265|1=Misogi}} before landing. This is sometimes said to be gender discrimination, but there is a theory that the island's god is a female god ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tashin Himekami|1=UNKNOWN}}) and that women who land on the island are said to be jealous and have a curse, but this is not confirmed. Excavations on Okinoshima Island have been carried out for more than ten years since 1952, and a large amount of ritual artifacts (offerings) such as ancient ritual remains and ornaments from the 4th to 9th centuries were discovered, as well as stone tools, pottery, and other artifacts from the {{ill|lt=Jomon period|Q52824|WD=Q52824|1=Jōmon period}} to the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. For this reason, Okinoshima is commonly called the ``{{ill|lt=Shosoin|Q2379007|WD=Q2379007|1=Shōsōin}}'' of the sea, and it is remembered that it has been the subject of {{ill|lt=faith|Q5410500|WD=Q5410500|1=Faith}} by {{ill|lt=Amajin|Q9495537|WD=Q9495537|1=Ama People}} and others since prehistoric times. Currently, it is designated as an emergency evacuation port during typhoons. The plaque of {{ill|lt=Divine Rescript|Q11588781|WD=Q11588781|1=Commandment}} that is hung in the shrine's worship hall is {{ill|lt=Calligraphy|Q11498466|WD=Q11498466|1=Calligraphy}} by {{ill|lt=Prince Fushiminomiya Sadaai|Q466326|WD=Q466326|1=Prince Fushimi Sadanaru}}, and the plaque at Munakata Palace is the script of Imperial Envoy Shonii Gon Dainagon, Akitaka Hamuro.{{ill|lt=Egypt|Q79|WD=Q79|1=Egypt}}{{ill|lt=Archaeologist|Q3621491|WD=Q3621491|1=Archaeologist}} {{ill|lt=Sakuji Yoshimura|Q2740406|WD=Q2740406|1=Sakuji Yoshimura}} advocated A movement arose to designate the ritual sites of Noshima and the Munakata region as {{ill|lt=World Heritage|Q9259|WD=Q9259|1=World Heritage Site}}, and in 2009, "Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, Hetsu-miya" and "Okitsu-miya Yohaisho" were established. Donated by the Kuroda clan, the lord of Fukuoka domain.) * Torii, et al. === History ===In {{ill|lt=tradition|Q36192|WD=Q36192|1=Folklore}}, it has {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=origin|1=UNKNOWN}} in {{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|1=Japanese mythology}}. {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}} and {{ill|lt=Susanoo|Q272993|WD=Q272993|lt=Amaterasu and Susa|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} During Noo's Pledge|Q11284880|Pledge}} (Pledge), Amaterasu Omikami bit down the Sword of Suho, and the three goddesses of Munakata were born from the fragments that blew out. It was built with a donation from {{ill|lt=Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431|WD=Q7429431|1=Sazō Idemitsu}}, a businessman whom he admired, and he worked hard to encourage the government to investigate and excavate the Okinoshima ritual ruins where Okitsu Shrine is located. === Kei Yukiyuki === {{ill|lt=1983|Q2434|WD=Q2434|1=1983}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}58), Crown Prince Akihito (later {{ill|lt=Emperor Empress Akihito|UNKNOWN|lt=Retired Emperor Akihito}}) and his wife Michiko (later {{ill|lt=Emperor Empress Michiko|Q87610|WD=Q87610|1=Empress Michiko}}) visited Hetsu Shrine. {{ill|lt=2013|Q1998|WD=Q1998|1=2013}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}25), {{ill|lt=Naruhito|Q217096|WD=Q217096|lt=Crown Prince Naruhito|1=Naruhito}} visited Hetsu Shrine. {{ill|lt=2017|Q25290|WD=Q25290|1=2017}} (2017) {{ill|lt=October 29|Q2951|WD=Q2951|1=October 29}}, Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko became the first emperors and empresses in history to visit Hetsu Shrine to pay their respects.{{Cite news|Japanese book|title=Fukuoka) Their Majesties visit Munakata Taisha, a World Heritage Site: Asahi Shimbun Digital|url=https://www.asahi.com/sp/articles/ASKBY5R38KBYTIPE012.html|accessdate=2018-05-08|language=ja-JP|work=Asahi Shimbun Digital}}{{Broken link|date=March 2024}}. In addition, as a member of the imperial family, {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|WD=Q34479|1=Hirohito}}'s younger brother {{ill|lt=archaeologist|Q3621491|WD=Q3621491|1=Archaeologist}} {{ill|lt=Prince Takahito Mikasa|Q280229|WD=Q280229|1=Takahito, Prince Mikasa}} visited the shrine many times, and he also composed waka poems about Okinoshima. === Sessha === * Kamiminato Munakata Shrine (Old Shrine) - Outside the precincts of the shrine (Autumn Grand Festival Tajima Hojokai, {{ill|lt=Miare Festival|Q11278738|WD=Q11278738|1=Miare Festival}}, where mikoshi of the three goddesses are lined up and dedicated) === Shinto rituals and festivals === * New Year's Festival - Shinto rituals to celebrate the New Year, such as Saidan Festival. 1st to 3rd of New Year every year. * Spring Festival - April 1st-3rd every year. * Summer Purification - Held at the end of July every year. * {{ill|lt=Tanabata|Q13423122|WD=Q13423122|1=Qixi Festival}} Festival - Held every year on {{ill|lt=lunar calendar|Q11511066|WD=Q11511066|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar}} at the evening of July 7th at the Nakatsu Shrine of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chikuzen Oshima|1=UNKNOWN}}. There are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kengyu|1=UNKNOWN}}sha and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Orijo|1=UNKNOWN}}sha, in front of which bamboo bamboo leaves with strips of paper are erected to pray for improvement in the craft. A ritual is held to predict the fate of men and women by looking at their reflections in the water, and a Tanabata {{ill|lt=calligraphy|Q11498466|WD=Q11498466|1=calligraphy}} competition is also held. According to the Shohei Annual Events, it is {{ill|lt=1346|Q6080|WD=Q6080|1=1346}} ``Tanabata Mushifuri Shinto ritual on the seventh day of July''. * Autumn Festival - October 1st to 3rd every year. Prior to the event at Hetsu Shrine's main shrine on the 1st to 3rd, there is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine welcome|1=UNKNOWN}} ritual held at Nakatsu-miya and Okitsu-miya shrines, and a {{ill|lt=divine celebration|UNKNOWN|lt=marine divine celebration}} is held with colorful flags and banners set up by fishing boats (Miare Festival). At the main shrine, {{ill|lt=Okina|Q11610439|WD=Q11610439|1=okina}} dances, customary dances, {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}}, dedication {{ill|lt=sumo|Q40561|WD=Q40561|1=Sumo}}, etc. are performed. Its origins date back to the {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, and its official name is ``Tajima Hojokai.'' * Kencha Festival - Held on October 17th every year. * Harvest Festival - A new festival that began to be held every year after the Heisei Emperor and Empress paid their respects to our company.* West Japan Chrysanthemum Exhibition - A chrysanthemum exhibition held every November. A large number of cultivated chrysanthemums from Kyushu and other prefectures in western Japan will be on display and appreciated. * Ancient Ceremony Festival, Hibisai Festival - A secret winter festival with a history of over 800 years that is held in mid-December every year. * New Year's Purification - New Year's Eve Shinto ritual held on New Year's Eve every year. === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * '''Items excavated from the Okitsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture/Traditional Items excavated from the Oki-tsu-miya ritual site of Munakata Taisha Shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture'''' Bulk: A collection of artifacts excavated from over 20 ritual sites on Okinoshima, a remote island in the Genkai Sea. It was excavated during the first to third excavations from {{ill|lt=1954|Q18581|WD=Q18581|1=1954}} to {{ill|lt=1971|Q2475|WD=Q2475|1=1971}}. Spreads from {{ill|lt=Kofun period|Q459939|WD=Q459939|1=Kofun period}} to {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}} ({{ill|lt=4th century|Q8099|WD=Q8099|1=4th century}} to {{ill|lt=10th century|Q8052|WD=Q8052|1=10th century}}). The main artifacts excavated include various bronze mirrors, horse harnesses made of gilt bronze (gold plated on copper), including products from China and the Korean Peninsula, as well as Haji ware, Sansai pottery, talcum products, jade items, and swords. Among the excavated items are fragments of glass bowls thought to have been made by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Persia|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sassanid|Q83891|WD=Q83891|1=Sasanian Empire}}. It is an extremely valuable academic resource that contributes to research in a variety of fields, including archaeology, art history, religious history, and ancient history. The results of three excavations have been published in the form of reports called ``Okinoshima,'' ``Zoku Okinoshima,'' and ``Munakata Okinoshima.'' These excavated items are on display at the sacred treasure museum of Munakata Taisha Shrine. In {{ill|lt=1962|Q2764|WD=Q2764|1=1962}}, the artifacts from the first and second excavations were designated as national treasures, and in {{ill|lt=2003|Q1986|WD=Q1986|1=2003}}, the artifacts from the third excavation were additionally designated as national treasures. It is the largest national treasure in Japan in terms of quantity, consisting of approximately 80,000 relics. === Important cultural property === * Munakata Shrine Hetsumiya Worship Hall * Munakata Shrine Hetsumiya Main Hall * A pair of wooden guardian dogs * A pair of stone guardian dogs * Aikawa Odoka Tajiro Doumaru with helmet and pot sleeves - "{{ill|lt=Doumaru|Q495328|WD=Q495328|1=Dō-maru}}" is a type of armor. * Sutra stone (Front {{ill|lt=Amida Tathagata|Q236242|WD=Q236242|1=Amitābha}} statue, back {{ill|lt=Amida Sutra|Q2661817|WD=Q2661817|1=Amitābha Sūtra}}) (Amida Buddha sutra monument) * Munakata Shrine Documents Volume 12 with attached: Munakata Shrine Records Volume 5, 1 volume, Munakata Shrine Documents Somokuroki 1 volume * 4,342 volumes of Shirojoboshi's Isshu Issukyo When it was designated as an important cultural property in 1958, there were 4,331 volumes, but 11 volumes were additionally designated in 1992 (Ministry of Education Notification No. 85, June 22, 1992). Colophon from 1187 to 1227 (Owned by Koshoji Temple, Tajima, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) * Talcstone sutra cylinder inscribed in the 4th year of the Ninpei era (owned by Inamoto Ward, Munakata City, managed by Munakata Taisha Shrine) === Historic Site (Nationally Designated) === * Munakata Shrine grounds === Fukuoka Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === * Munakata Shrine Nakatsumiya Main Hall === Others === * Compass of {{ill|lt=Battleship|Q182531|WD=Q182531|1=Battleship}}{{ill|lt=Mikasa (battleship)|Q696891|WD=Q696891|lt=Mikasa|1=Japanese battleship Mikasa}}, which was active in {{ill|lt=Battle of the Sea of Japan|Q208127|WD=Q208127|1=Battle of Tsushima}} * An Okina mask surfaced off the coast of Cape Kane in {{ill|lt=Meio|Q1193841|WD=Q1193841|1=Meiō}}8 ({{ill|lt=1499|Q6708|WD=Q6708|1=1499}}) === Munakata Taisha and Sazo Idemitsu ==={{ill|lt=Idemitsu Kosan|Q2216770|WD=Q2216770|1=Idemitsu Kosan}}'s founder, {{ill|lt=Sazo Idemitsu|Q7429431|WD=Q7429431|1=Sazō Idemitsu}}, is from the former {{ill|lt=Munakata District|Q6935606|WD=Q6935606|1=Munakata District, Fukuoka}} Akama-juku, and has revered Munakata Taisha Shrine since childhood. In 1937, when he visited Betsu Shrine, he lamented the devastation of the shrine, and in 1942 he called for the formation of the ``Munakata Shrine Restoration Society'' and became its first president. After suspending its activities during and after the war, it was reorganized as the Munakata Taisha Reconstruction Society in 1969. The restoration of the main shrine and worship hall of Hetsu Shrine was largely due to Sazo's donations, but as he declined out of fear, there were no traces of his name within the shrine grounds for a long time, but there are now exhibits honoring Sazo at Shinpokan and other places. In the novel "{{ill|lt=A Man Called a Pirate|Q16046027|WD=Q16046027|1=A Man Called Pirate}}," which is based on Sazo, upon {{ill|lt=defeat|Q11499267|WD=Q11499267|1=defeat}}, a separate shrine was established within the company. }}It is depicted praying to the three goddesses of Munakata Shrine, who have been praying for the protection of {{ill|lt=Japan|Q17|WD=Q17|1=Japan}} and the {{ill|lt=Japanese people|Q16782073|WD=Q16782073|1=Ethnic Japanese}}. Sazo wrote in his book that he believed that Ise Shrine was the ancestor of the imperial family, and Munakata Taisha Shrine was the ancestor of the people. {{ill|lt=Tokyo|Q1490|WD=Q1490|1=Tokyo}}{{ill|lt=Idemitsu Art Museum|Q3076590|WD=Q3076590|1=Idemitsu Museum of Arts}} located in {{ill|lt=Chiyoda-ku|Q214051|WD=Q214051|1=Chiyoda, Tokyo}} is an art museum that exhibits artworks collected by Sazo.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://idemitsu-museum.or.jp/about/outline/|title=About Idemitsu Museum of Art|accessdate=2024-09-24|website=Idemitsu Museum of Art website|publisher=Public The Idemitsu Museum of Art}} regularly holds special exhibitions such as the Munakata/Okinoshima Exhibition, and on October 17th every year, when the tea ceremony is held at Munakata Taisha Shrine, many of the famous tea utensils from the collection are put on display, and the {{ill|lt=Omotesenke|Q3278052|WD=Q3278052|1=Omotesenke}} master offers tea, commemorating the perpetuation of the shrine and remembering Sazo. === Specialty === * Munakata Taisha Shrine rice crackers * Happiness Mochi === Transportation === By bus * Hetsunomiya - From {{ill|lt=Kagoshima Main Line|Q1187520|WD=Q1187520|1=Kagoshima Main Line}}/{{ill|lt=Togo Station|Q5359652|WD=Q5359652|1=Tōgō Station}}, take {{ill|lt=Nishitetsu Bus|Q11629843|WD=Q11629843|1=Nishitetsu Bus}} Route 1 bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at "Munakata Taisha-mae". It takes 10 minutes. * Nakatsumiya/Okitsumiya Yohaisho - From Togo Station on the Kagoshima Main Line, take the Nishitetsu bus bound for Kamiminato Hatoba and get off at the last stop (20 minutes). From {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiminato Fishing Port|1=UNKNOWN}} to {{ill|lt=Oshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|Q30933915|WD=Q30933915|lt=Oshima Port|1=Port of Oshima}}, it takes 15 minutes by the {{ill|lt=Munakata Municipal Ferry|Q11451853|WD=Q11451853|1=Munakata Municipal Ferry}} passenger ship, or 25 minutes by ferry. 5 minutes walk (800 meters) from Oshima Port to Nakatsunomiya. If you have your own car, it is 16 kilometers from {{ill|lt=Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803|WD=Q1060803|1=Kyushu Expressway}}{{ill|lt=Wakamiya Interchange|Q1575782|WD=Q1575782|1=Wakamiya interchange}} to Hetsunomiya and 19 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. Alternatively, from the same {{ill|lt=Koga Interchange|Q1577981|WD=Q1577981|1=Koga interchange}}, it is 15 kilometers to Hetsunomiya and 17 kilometers to Kamiminato Fishing Port. From Kamiminato Fishing Port, take the Munakata Municipal Ferry to Oshima Port, 400 meters to Nakatsu-miya Shrine, and 2.3 kilometers to Okitsu-miya Yohaisho. === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 59 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, 327 pages * Shunpei Ueyama et al., “Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines” {{ill|lt=Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312|WD=Q11501312|1=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha. The former {{ill|lt=Shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System #Government Shrine|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, and currently it is {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. There are over 7,000 shrines throughout Japan, including {{ill|lt=Munakata Shrine|Q11451876|WD=Q11451876|1=Munakata Shrines}}, {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|WD=Q191763|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, and {{ill|lt=Munakata Three Goddess It is the headquarters of the shrine that enshrines|Q10948069|WD=Q10948069|1=Three Munakata Goddesses}}, and in ``{{ill|lt=Nihon Shoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', it is referred to as ``''Doshu Taka''''. {{ill|lt=Okinoshima|Q7082047|WD=Q7082047|1=Okinoshima (Fukuoka)}} floating in the {{ill|lt=Genkai Sea|Q498047|WD=Q498047|1=Genkai Sea}} is considered a sacred area, and many of the {{ill|lt=ancient|Q41493|WD=Q41493|1=Ancient history}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rituals|1=UNKNOWN}} offerings excavated on Okinoshima have been designated as {{ill|lt=national treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}. It is also called ``Ura Ise''.It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in {{ill|lt=2017|Q25290|WD=Q25290|1=2017}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}29) as one of the constituent assets of '''{{ill|lt="Island inhabited by the Gods" Munakata/Okinoshima and Related Heritage Group|Q324638|WD=Q324638|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region}}'''. === Overview === Munakata Taisha is a general term for three shrines: ``Okitsu-miya'' on {{ill|lt=Okinoshima|Q7082047|WD=Q7082047|1=Okinoshima (Fukuoka)}}, ``Nakatsu-miya'' on {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chikuzen Oshima|1=UNKNOWN}}, and ``Hetsu-miya'' (Soja) on Tajima, {{ill|lt=Munakata City|Q819603|WD=Q819603|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, but nowadays it often refers to just ``Hetsu-miya''. Hetsu Shrine is enshrined in Tajima, Munakata City, and is also called ``Tajima-sama'' by the locals. There is also Okitsu-miya Yohaisho ('''Teitsu-miya'') on Chikuzen Oshima. On the map, Nakatsu-miya, which is 11 km away from Hetsu-miya, and Okitsu-miya, which is 49 km further away, are all in a straight line. It is one of the oldest shrines in Japan, whose history is recorded in the {{ill|lt=Kikiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}, and has been a maritime route for politics, economy, and culture between the continent and the peninsula since ancient times. Since ancient times, he has been worshiped for his divine power as a {{ill|lt=god|Q178885|WD=Q178885|1=Deity}} of {{ill|lt=sea surface|Q125465|WD=Q125465|lt=sea|1=Sea level}} and {{ill|lt=traffic safety|Q1147899|WD=Q1147899|1=Road safety}}, but now he is worshiped not only on the sea but also on all roads, land, and traffic safety under the name of Doshu Taka.{{ill|lt=faith|Q5410500|WD=Q5410500|1=Faith}}. For this reason, many {{ill|lt=cars|Q1420|WD=Q1420|1=Car}} with Munakata Taisha Shrine {{ill|lt=stickers|Q2872553|WD=Q2872553|lt=stickers|1=Sticker}} can be seen in Fukuoka Prefecture and its surrounding areas, and there are also a large number of people who purchase a new car and receive a purification at the prayer hall. Additionally, the traffic safety charms that are worn on cars originate from Munakata Taisha Shrine.Okinoshima Island, where Okitsu-miya is located, is located at a key point for maritime traffic.Since ancient times, people have been called ``Oiwasama'' because people were not allowed to enter the island and reveal what they saw or heard, and the entire island is {{ill|lt=go|Q11488760|WD=Q11488760|1=御}}{{ill|lt=divine body|Q327532|WD=Q327532|1=Shintai}}. For this reason, even today {{ill|lt=women are prohibited|Q11446290|WD=Q11446290|1=Nyonin Kinsei}}, and even men must undergo {{ill|lt=misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265|1=Misogi}} before landing. This is sometimes said to be gender discrimination, but there is a theory that the island's god is a female god ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tashin Himekami|1=UNKNOWN}}) and that women who land on the island are said to be jealous and have a curse, but this is not confirmed. Excavations on Okinoshima Island have been carried out for more than ten years since 1952, and a large amount of ritual artifacts (offerings) such as ancient ritual remains and ornaments from the 4th to 9th centuries were discovered, as well as stone tools, pottery, and other artifacts from the {{ill|lt=Jomon period|Q52824|WD=Q52824|1=Jōmon period}} to the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. For this reason, Okinoshima is commonly called the ``{{ill|lt=Shosoin|Q2379007|WD=Q2379007|1=Shōsōin}}'' of the sea, and it is remembered that it has been the subject of {{ill|lt=faith|Q5410500|WD=Q5410500|1=Faith}} by {{ill|lt=Amajin|Q9495537|WD=Q9495537|1=Ama People}} and others since prehistoric times. Currently, it is designated as an emergency evacuation port during typhoons. The plaque of {{ill|lt=Divine Rescript|Q11588781|WD=Q11588781|1=Commandment}} that is hung in the shrine's worship hall is {{ill|lt=Calligraphy|Q11498466|WD=Q11498466|1=Calligraphy}} by {{ill|lt=Prince Fushiminomiya Sadaai|Q466326|WD=Q466326|1=Prince Fushimi Sadanaru}}, and the plaque at Munakata Palace is the script of Imperial Envoy Shonii Gon Dainagon, Akitaka Hamuro.{{ill|lt=Egypt|Q79|WD=Q79|1=Egypt}}{{ill|lt=Archaeologist|Q3621491|WD=Q3621491|1=Archaeologist}} {{ill|lt=Sakuji Yoshimura|Q2740406|WD=Q2740406|1=Sakuji Yoshimura}} advocated A movement arose to designate the ritual sites of Noshima and the Munakata region as {{ill|lt=World Heritage|Q9259|WD=Q9259|1=World Heritage Site}}, and in 2009, "Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, Hetsu-miya" and "Okitsu-miya Yohaisho" were established. It was added to the tentative list as a group of related heritage sites including the ``Island inhabited by the Gods,'' Munakata/Okinoshima, and was nominated in 2015, and in July 2017, it was officially registered as a World Heritage Site at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=UNESCO|1=UNKNOWN}} World Heritage Committee meeting in {{ill|lt=Poland|Q36|WD=Q36|1=Poland}} and {{ill|lt=Krakow|Q31487|WD=Q31487|1=Kraków}}. === Enshrined God === Each of the three shrines enshrines the following gods, collectively known as {{ill|lt=Three Goddesses of Munakata|Q10948069|WD=Q10948069|1=Three Munakata Goddesses}} (Munakata Okami). * Okitsuguu Shrine: {{ill|lt=Takiribime|Q10932870|WD=Q10932870|lt=Tashin Himekami|1=Tagorihime}} * Nakatsugu Shrine: {{ill|lt=Tagitsuhime|Q10932592|WD=Q10932592|lt=Tanatsu Himekami|1=Tagitsuhime}} * Hetsu Shrine: {{ill|lt=Ichikishima Hime|Q11059454|WD=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishima Himekami|1=Ichikishima-hime}} File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Hetsu Shrine).JPG|Hetsu Shrine Worship Hall (photo before the construction of the shrine) File:Haiden of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Nakatsu Shrine Worship Hall File:Munakata Taisha Okitsu Shrine.JPG|Okitsu Shrine Worship Hall === Shrine building === [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden1.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Worship Hall]] [[File:Munakata-taisha haiden2.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsu-miya Hall of Worship]] [[File:Munakata-taisha shimboku.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Sacred Tree]] [[File:Munakata-taisha museum.jpg|Thumbnail|Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya Shinpokan]] === Munakata Taisha Hetsumiya === * Main shrine (first shrine, Ichikishima Hime is the enshrined deity. Donated by the Kuroda clan, the lord of Fukuoka domain.) * Torii, et al. === History ===In {{ill|lt=tradition|Q36192|WD=Q36192|1=Folklore}}, it has {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=origin|1=UNKNOWN}} in {{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|1=Japanese mythology}}. {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}} and {{ill|lt=Susanoo|Q272993|WD=Q272993|lt=Amaterasu and Susa|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} During Noo's Pledge|Q11284880|Pledge}} (Pledge), Amaterasu Omikami bit down the Sword of Suho, and the three goddesses of Munakata were born from the fragments that blew out. The origin of Munakata Taisha Shrine is said to be that the goddesses worshiped Amaterasu's ``''{{ill|lt=divine edict|Q11588781|WD=Q11588781|1=Commandment}}'''' and descended to the islands of Tsukushi Munakata in the Genkai Sea in the Kaihoku region to protect and help the imperial descendant {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, and came to rule over this land. The only ``gods who descended from heaven to earth'' mentioned in {{ill|lt=Kiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}} are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} and the three goddesses of Munakata who descended from heaven before {{ill|lt=Descent of Tenson|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733|1=Tenson kōrin}}. This is the oldest record of the Kiki in which the names of gods and their enshrined locations are clearly described. According to the {{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664|1=Chikuzen Province}}{{ill|lt=Fudōki|Q1194534|WD=Q1194534|1=Fudoki}} regarding the shrine worship of Munakata Sangu Shrine, ``Saikaido Fudoki says, ``Since the time of Saimon Mountain, where Munakata Okami and his god were descended, , Ao-tama-Okikutsu-miya-no-omote, eight-shaku-purple-purple-oki-Okitsu-miya-no-omote, Yata-kagami-Okibetsu-miya-no-omote, and these three tables are placed in the form of the god's body. There is an anecdote that says, ``Sannomiya, Soku-no-in, Gin-gata-gun, Gonin-kai, descendants of Munakata Ki-Okai-no-Mikoto, and now Munakata Ason, etc.'' In ``{{ill|lt=Kojiki|Q813031|WD=Q813031|1=Kojiki}}'', Munakata is given the character ``Musakata,'' and is also written ``Munetakata'' or ``Munakata,'' but there is also a theory that it was originally Mizugata. It has been worshiped as the guardian deity of the local people since ancient times, and it is said that when {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} prayed for safe voyages during her {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}}, she had a miraculous experience here, and it is said that she had a habit of sending envoys to Munakata whenever the situation arises. It was valued by the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamato Imperial Court|1=UNKNOWN}}, and since ancient times, whenever the capital was transferred, a spirit of our company was enshrined in the {{ill|lt=kendokoro|Q11635085|WD=Q11635085|1=Kashiko-dokoro}} (kashikodokoro) of the imperial court. This anecdote also reveals how he came to be worshiped as a {{ill|lt=guardian|Q131278957|WD=Q131278957|1=Guardian deities}} of safe navigation.With the introduction of {{ill|lt=ritsuryo system#Japanese ritsuryo system|Q742460|WD=Q742460|lt=ritsuryo system|1=Ritsuryō}}, {{ill|lt=kokugunri system|Q11421491|WD=Q11421491|lt=kokugun system|1=province-district-township system}}, {{ill|lt=Munakata county|Q6935606|WD=Q6935606|lt=one county of Munakata|1=Munakata District, Fukuoka}} was given as {{ill|lt=Temple territory|Q11458058|WD=Q11458058|lt=Shinryo|1=Jisha-ryō}}, The local {{ill|lt=gozoku|Q84066|WD=Q84066|1=Gōzoku}}{{ill|lt=Munakata clan|Q16481907|WD=Q16481907|lt=Munegata clan|1=Munakata clan}} served the shrine as {{ill|lt=Shinto priest|Q60523|WD=Q60523|lt=Shinto priest|1=Kannushi}}, and also took charge of the {{ill|lt=administration|Q31728|WD=Q31728|1=Public administration}} of {{ill|lt=Kamigun|Q11590937|WD=Q11590937|1=Kamigun}}. The current Hetsu Shrine {{ill|lt=main hall|Q2044994|WD=Q2044994|1=Honden}}, with its beautiful large shingled roof, was rebuilt by the chief priest {{ill|lt=Ujisada Munakata|Q10204112|WD=Q10204112|1=Munakata Ujisada}} in the 6th year of Tensho ({{ill|lt=1578|Q6707|WD=Q6707|1=1578}}).
